1	"""undo <op_id>: apply the inverse of one subtree delete to the graph as it is now.
2	
3	Order of work:
4	
5	1. The delete's removed nodes, parents first. For each: decide restored, merged or skipped; make the
6	   change; decide the arrow from its parent; refresh the tags of the node and everything below it.
7	2. The delete's remaining removed arrows (the references ones), each decided the same way.
8	3. Rows of earlier undos that are waiting on this delete, newest journal first, parents first.
9	4. The report, printed from the journal rows.
10	
11	The undo is logged as an operation of its own the first time it runs ('undo:<op_id>', by a person), and
12	every journal row records which undo decided it. A merge also records what the live node held before (the
13	row's `prior`), and the report lists any written value it replaced. That is what a redo will need.
14	
15	Each row is one step and one transaction: its graph change, its tag refresh and its outcome in the journal
16	are saved together or not at all. A row that already has an outcome is never decided again, so a second run
17	writes nothing and a run that resumes after a crash carries on where the last committed step left off.
18	Each decision looks only at the live graph and the journal, so the resumed run decides as an uninterrupted
19	run would have.
20	
21	Node decision
22	    name used by a live node      -> merged into that node (reason name_in_use)
23	    else parent live (or merged)  -> restored with its old id and all its fields
24	    else                          -> skipped, reason parent_not_live, waiting_on the delete holding the parent
25	    no parent at delete time      -> restored at the top level (when the name is free)
26	
27	Merge, field by field (description, owner, tags, and type): the most recent write wins. The seed counts as
28	written at seq 0; a value put back by an undo keeps the seq of its original write. Everything in a journal
29	was written before its delete, and anything written on a live node after the delete is newer, so a value a
30	person wrote after the delete is never replaced. effective_tags is never filled: it is recomputed.
31	
32	Arrow decision, after resolving each end to where it is now (same id, the node it was merged into, or not
33	live), first match wins:
34	    an end is not live                       -> skipped endpoint_not_live (waiting_on that end's delete)
35	    the arrow already exists                 -> merged already_present
36	    contains, and the child has a parent     -> skipped child_has_other_parent (the later placement wins)
37	    a person re-pointed it away after delete -> skipped removed_by_person
38	    contains, and it would close a loop      -> skipped would_create_cycle
39	    otherwise                                -> added: restored (same ends) or merged endpoint_merged
40	"""
41	
42	from __future__ import annotations
43	
44	import json
45	from dataclasses import dataclass
46	from typing import Any
47	
48	from .common import CONTAINS, HUMAN, WRITTEN_FIELDS, tags_json
49	from .graph import ancestor_or_self, edge_live, has_parent, insert_edge, log_op, node_live, record_write
50	from .store import Store
51	from .tags import refresh_subtree
52	
53	RESTORED, MERGED, SKIPPED = "restored", "merged", "skipped"
54	Edge = tuple[str, str, str]
55	
56	NODE_ROW_SQL = """
57	SELECT delete_op, id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, parent_id, writes, outcome, waiting_on
58	FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND id = ?
59	"""
60	
61	
62	class UndoError(Exception):
63	    """undo was asked for something it cannot do. Nothing has been written."""
64	
65	
66	@dataclass(frozen=True)
67	class Place:
68	    """Where a node id is now: a live id, or not live and the delete that has to be undone first."""
69	
70	    live_id: str | None
71	    waiting_on: str | None = None
72	
73	
74	@dataclass(frozen=True)
75	class NodeRow:
76	    delete_op: str
77	    id: str
78	    qualified_name: str
79	    type: str
80	    description: str | None
81	    owner: str | None
82	    tags: str
83	    parent_id: str | None
84	    writes: str
85	    outcome: str | None
86	    waiting_on: str | None
87	
88	
89	def _pending(outcome: str | None, row_waiting_on: str | None, retrying_for: str | None) -> bool:
90	    """A row still to decide: no outcome yet, or (when retrying) skipped while waiting on this delete."""
91	    if retrying_for is None:
92	        return outcome is None
93	    return outcome == SKIPPED and row_waiting_on == retrying_for
94	
95	
96	async def undo(store: Store, op_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
97	    """Undo one subtree delete and return its report."""
98	    op = await store.fetchone("SELECT kind, status FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (op_id,))
99	    if op is None:
100	        raise UndoError(f"no operation with op_id {op_id!r}")
101	    kind, status = op
102	    if kind != "delete_subtree":
103	        raise UndoError(f"{op_id} is {kind!r}, not a delete_subtree; undo takes the op_id of a subtree delete")
104	    if status != "applied":
105	        raise UndoError(f"{op_id} was rejected when it was applied, so it removed nothing")
106	    run = UndoRun(store, op_id)
107	    async with store.transaction():  # logged once; a resumed or repeated run finds it and writes nothing
108	        if not await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (run.undo_id,)):
109	            await log_op(store, run.undo_id, "undo", HUMAN, {"undo_of": op_id})
110	    await run.run()
111	    return await build_report(store, op_id)
112	
113	
114	class UndoRun:
115	    def __init__(self, store: Store, op_id: str) -> None:
116	        self.store = store
117	        self.op_id = op_id
118	        self.undo_id = f"undo:{op_id}"  # written next to every outcome this run decides
119	
120	    async def run(self) -> None:
121	        await self._decide_rows(self.op_id, retrying_for=None)
122	        await self.retry_waiting()
123	
124	    async def retry_waiting(self) -> None:
125	        """Rows of earlier undos that were skipped because this delete held a node they need.
126	
127	        A row can only be blocked by its own journal or a newer one (everything it needs was live when its
128	        delete ran), so newer journals go first, and inside a journal nodes parents first, then arrows.
129	        """
130	        journals = await self.store.fetchall(
131	            """
132	            SELECT w.delete_op FROM (
133	                SELECT delete_op FROM removed_nodes WHERE outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?1
134	                UNION
135	                SELECT delete_op FROM removed_edges WHERE outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?1
136	            ) w JOIN ops o ON o.op_id = w.delete_op
137	            ORDER BY o.seq DESC
138	            """,
139	            (self.op_id,),
140	        )
141	        for (delete_op,) in journals:
142	            await self._decide_rows(delete_op, retrying_for=self.op_id)
143	
144	    async def _decide_rows(self, delete_op: str, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
145	        """The pending rows of one journal: nodes parents first, then arrows, one step each."""
146	        if retrying_for is None:
147	            where, params = "outcome IS NULL", (delete_op,)
148	        else:
149	            where, params = "outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?", (delete_op, retrying_for)
150	        nodes = await self.store.fetchall(
151	            f"SELECT id FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND {where} ORDER BY ord", params
152	        )
153	        for (node_id,) in nodes:
154	            await self.node_step(delete_op, node_id, retrying_for)
155	        edges = await self.store.fetchall(
156	            f"SELECT from_id, to_id, type FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? AND {where} ORDER BY ord", params
157	        )
158	        for from_id, to_id, edge_type in edges:
159	            await self.edge_step(delete_op, (from_id, to_id, edge_type), retrying_for)
160	
161	    # ---- steps -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
162	
163	    async def node_step(self, delete_op: str, node_id: str, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
164	        """One removed node and the arrow from its parent, in one transaction."""
165	        store = self.store
166	        async with store.transaction():
167	            row = await self._node_row(delete_op, node_id)
168	            if row is None or not _pending(row.outcome, row.waiting_on, retrying_for):
169	                return
170	            parent_arrow = (row.parent_id, row.id, CONTAINS) if row.parent_id is not None else None
171	            holder = await store.fetchval("SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE qualified_name = ?", (row.qualified_name,))
172	            if holder is not None:
173	                detail, prior = await self._merge_into(row, holder)
174	                await self._mark_node(row, MERGED, "name_in_use", merged_into=holder, detail=detail, prior=prior)
175	                target = holder
176	            else:
177	                if parent_arrow is not None:
178	                    parent = await self.where(parent_arrow[0])
179	                    if parent.live_id is None:
180	                        await self._mark_node(row, SKIPPED, "parent_not_live", waiting_on=parent.waiting_on)
181	                        await self._mark_edge(
182	                            delete_op, parent_arrow, SKIPPED, "endpoint_not_live", waiting_on=parent.waiting_on
183	                        )
184	                        return
185	                await store.write(
186	                    "INSERT INTO nodes (id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, effective_tags) "
187	                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, '[]')",
188	                    (row.id, row.qualified_name, row.type, row.description, row.owner, row.tags),
189	                )
190	                await self._mark_node(row, RESTORED)
191	                target = row.id
192	            if parent_arrow is not None and await self._edge_pending(delete_op, parent_arrow, retrying_for):
193	                await self._decide_edge(delete_op, parent_arrow)
194	            # Recompute what this step can have changed: the node and everything now below it.
195	            await refresh_subtree(store, target)
196	
197	    async def edge_step(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
198	        """One removed arrow, in one transaction."""
199	        async with self.store.transaction():
200	            if not await self._edge_pending(delete_op, edge, retrying_for):
201	                return
202	            added = await self._decide_edge(delete_op, edge)
203	            if added is not None and edge[2] == CONTAINS:
204	                await refresh_subtree(self.store, added[1])
205	
206	    # ---- decisions ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    async def where(self, node_id: str) -> Place:
209	        """The live node that stands for node_id now, or the delete that has to be undone first.
210	
211	        Follows merges (a merged id lives on as the node it was folded into). A node only disappears through
212	        a delete, so a node that is not live is always held by some journal row.
213	        """
214	        current = node_id
215	        seen: set[str] = set()
216	        while current not in seen:
217	            seen.add(current)
218	            if await node_live(self.store, current):
219	                return Place(current)
220	            rows = await self.store.fetchall(
221	                "SELECT r.outcome, r.merged_into, r.waiting_on, r.delete_op "
222	                "FROM removed_nodes r JOIN ops o ON o.op_id = r.delete_op WHERE r.id = ? ORDER BY o.seq DESC",
223	                (current,),
224	            )
225	            merged = next((r for r in rows if r[0] == MERGED), None)
226	            if merged is not None:
227	                current = merged[1]
228	                continue
229	            holder = next((r for r in rows if r[0] is None or r[0] == SKIPPED), None)
230	            if holder is None:
231	                return Place(None)
232	            outcome, _, waiting_on, delete_op = holder
233	            # Held by a delete nobody has undone yet, or by a row that is itself waiting on another delete.
234	            return Place(None, delete_op if outcome is None else waiting_on)
235	        return Place(None)
236	
237	    async def _decide_edge(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
238	        """Decide one removed arrow and write the outcome. Returns the arrow added, if one was."""
239	        store = self.store
240	        from_id, to_id, edge_type = edge
241	        ends = (await self.where(from_id), await self.where(to_id))
242	        if any(end.live_id is None for end in ends):
243	            waiting_on = next((end.waiting_on for end in ends if end.live_id is None and end.waiting_on), None)
244	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "endpoint_not_live", waiting_on=waiting_on)
245	            return None
246	        now = (ends[0].live_id, ends[1].live_id)
247	        assert now[0] is not None and now[1] is not None
248	        if await edge_live(store, now[0], now[1], edge_type):
249	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, MERGED, "already_present", now=now)
250	            return None
251	        if edge_type == CONTAINS and await has_parent(store, now[1]):
252	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "child_has_other_parent", now=now)
253	            return None
254	        if await store.fetchval(
255	            "SELECT 1 FROM edge_removals WHERE from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ? AND actor = 'human' "
256	            "AND seq > (SELECT seq FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?) LIMIT 1",
257	            (*now, edge_type, delete_op),
258	        ):
259	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "removed_by_person", now=now)
260	            return None
261	        if edge_type == CONTAINS and await ancestor_or_self(store, now[1], now[0]):
262	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "would_create_cycle", now=now)
263	            return None
264	        await insert_edge(store, now[0], now[1], edge_type)
265	        if now == (from_id, to_id):
266	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, RESTORED)
267	        else:
268	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, MERGED, "endpoint_merged", now=now)
269	        return now
270	
271	    async def _merge_into(self, row: NodeRow, holder: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
272	        """Fold a removed node into the live node that holds its name.
273	
274	        Returns the report detail, and `prior`: for every field whose value or write record changes, what the
275	        live node held before ({"value": ..., "write": [seq, actor] or null}), so a redo can put it back.
276	        """
277	        store = self.store
278	        live = await store.fetchone("SELECT type, description, owner, tags FROM nodes WHERE id = ?", (holder,))
279	        assert live is not None
280	        live_values = {"type": live[0], "description": live[1], "owner": live[2], "tags": json.loads(live[3])}
281	        old_values = {
282	            "type": row.type,
283	            "description": row.description,
284	            "owner": row.owner,
285	            "tags": json.loads(row.tags),
286	        }
287	        live_writes = {
288	            field: (seq, actor)
289	            for field, seq, actor in await store.fetchall(
290	                "SELECT field, seq, actor FROM field_writes WHERE node_id = ?", (holder,)
291	            )
292	        }
293	        old_writes = {field: (seq, actor) for field, (seq, actor) in json.loads(row.writes).items()}
294	
295	        filled: list[str] = []
296	        kept_live: list[str] = []
297	        not_restored: dict[str, Any] = {}
298	        take_value: list[str] = []
299	        take_write: list[str] = []
300	        for field in WRITTEN_FIELDS:
301	            old_w, live_w = old_writes.get(field), live_writes.get(field)
302	            old_is_newer = old_w is not None and (live_w is None or old_w[0] > live_w[0])
303	            differs = old_values[field] != live_values[field]
304	            if field == "type" and not differs:
305	                # Same type either way: nothing to report. Keep the newest report time for later merges.
306	                if old_is_newer:
307	                    take_write.append(field)
308	                continue
309	            if old_is_newer:
310	                filled.append(field)
311	                take_value.append(field)
312	                take_write.append(field)
313	            else:
314	                kept_live.append(field)
315	                if old_w is not None and differs:
316	                    not_restored[field] = old_values[field]
317	
318	        prior = {
319	            field: {"value": live_values[field], "write": list(live_writes[field]) if field in live_writes else None}
320	            for field in take_write
321	        }
322	        # A filled field that overwrote a value someone had written on the live node: show what was there.
323	        replaced = {
324	            field: live_values[field]
325	            for field in take_value
326	            if field in live_writes and live_values[field] != old_values[field]
327	        }
328	        if take_value:
329	            assignments = ", ".join(f"{field} = ?" for field in take_value)
330	            params = [tags_json(old_values[f]) if f == "tags" else old_values[f] for f in take_value]
331	            await store.write(f"UPDATE nodes SET {assignments} WHERE id = ?", (*params, holder))
332	        for field in take_write:
333	            seq, actor = old_writes[field]
334	            await record_write(store, holder, field, seq, actor)
335	        detail: dict[str, Any] = {"filled": filled, "kept_live": kept_live, "not_restored": not_restored}
336	        if replaced:
337	            detail["replaced"] = replaced
338	        return detail, prior
339	
340	    # ---- journal rows ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
341	
342	    async def _node_row(self, delete_op: str, node_id: str) -> NodeRow | None:
343	        row = await self.store.fetchone(NODE_ROW_SQL, (delete_op, node_id))
344	        return None if row is None else NodeRow(*row)
345	
346	    async def _edge_pending(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge, retrying_for: str | None) -> bool:
347	        row = await self.store.fetchone(
348	            "SELECT outcome, waiting_on FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? AND from_id = ? AND to_id = ? "
349	            "AND type = ?",
350	            (delete_op, *edge),
351	        )
352	        return row is not None and _pending(row[0], row[1], retrying_for)
353	
354	    async def _mark_node(
355	        self,
356	        row: NodeRow,
357	        outcome: str,
358	        reason: str | None = None,
359	        *,
360	        merged_into: str | None = None,
361	        waiting_on: str | None = None,
362	        detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
363	        prior: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
364	    ) -> None:
365	        await self.store.write(
366	            "UPDATE removed_nodes SET outcome = ?, reason = ?, merged_into = ?, waiting_on = ?, detail = ?, "
367	            "decided_by = ?, prior = ? WHERE delete_op = ? AND id = ?",
368	            (
369	                outcome,
370	                reason,
371	                merged_into,
372	                waiting_on,
373	                None if detail is None else json.dumps(detail, ensure_ascii=False),
374	                self.undo_id,

"""undo <op_id>: apply the inverse of one subtree delete to the graph as it is now.

Order of work:

1. The delete's removed nodes, parents first. For each: decide restored, merged or skipped; make the
   change; decide the arrow from its parent; refresh the tags of the node and everything below it.
2. The delete's remaining removed arrows (the references ones), each decided the same way.
3. Rows of earlier undos that are waiting on this delete, newest journal first, parents first.
4. The report, printed from the journal rows.

The undo is logged as an operation of its own the first time it runs ('undo:<op_id>', by a person), and
every journal row records which undo decided it. A merge also records what the live node held before (the
row's `prior`), and the report lists any written value it replaced. That is what a redo will need.

Each row is one step and one transaction: its graph change, its tag refresh and its outcome in the journal
are saved together or not at all. A row that already has an outcome is never decided again, so a second run
writes nothing and a run that resumes after a crash carries on where the last committed step left off.
Each decision looks only at the live graph and the journal, so the resumed run decides as an uninterrupted
run would have.

Node decision
    name used by a live node      -> merged into that node (reason name_in_use)
    else parent live (or merged)  -> restored with its old id and all its fields
    else                          -> skipped, reason parent_not_live, waiting_on the delete holding the parent
    no parent at delete time      -> restored at the top level (when the name is free)

Merge, field by field (description, owner, tags, and type): the most recent write wins. The seed counts as
written at seq 0; a value put back by an undo keeps the seq of its original write. Everything in a journal
was written before its delete, and anything written on a live node after the delete is newer, so a value a
person wrote after the delete is never replaced. effective_tags is never filled: it is recomputed.

Arrow decision, after resolving each end to where it is now (same id, the node it was merged into, or not
live), first match wins:
    an end is not live                       -> skipped endpoint_not_live (waiting_on that end's delete)
    the arrow already exists                 -> merged already_present
    contains, and the child has a parent     -> skipped child_has_other_parent (the later placement wins)
    a person re-pointed it away after delete -> skipped removed_by_person
    contains, and it would close a loop      -> skipped would_create_cycle
    otherwise                                -> added: restored (same ends) or merged endpoint_merged
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from .common import CONTAINS, HUMAN, WRITTEN_FIELDS, tags_json
from .graph import ancestor_or_self, edge_live, has_parent, insert_edge, log_op, node_live, record_write
from .store import Store
from .tags import refresh_subtree

RESTORED, MERGED, SKIPPED = "restored", "merged", "skipped"
Edge = tuple[str, str, str]

NODE_ROW_SQL = """
SELECT delete_op, id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, parent_id, writes, outcome, waiting_on
FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND id = ?
"""


class UndoError(Exception):
    """undo was asked for something it cannot do. Nothing has been written."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Place:
    """Where a node id is now: a live id, or not live and the delete that has to be undone first."""

    live_id: str | None
    waiting_on: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NodeRow:
    delete_op: str
    id: str
    qualified_name: str
    type: str
    description: str | None
    owner: str | None
    tags: str
    parent_id: str | None
    writes: str
    outcome: str | None
    waiting_on: str | None


def _pending(outcome: str | None, row_waiting_on: str | None, retrying_for: str | None) -> bool:
    """A row still to decide: no outcome yet, or (when retrying) skipped while waiting on this delete."""
    if retrying_for is None:
        return outcome is None
    return outcome == SKIPPED and row_waiting_on == retrying_for


async def undo(store: Store, op_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Undo one subtree delete and return its report."""
    op = await store.fetchone("SELECT kind, status FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (op_id,))
    if op is None:
        raise UndoError(f"no operation with op_id {op_id!r}")
    kind, status = op
    if kind != "delete_subtree":
        raise UndoError(f"{op_id} is {kind!r}, not a delete_subtree; undo takes the op_id of a subtree delete")
    if status != "applied":
        raise UndoError(f"{op_id} was rejected when it was applied, so it removed nothing")
    run = UndoRun(store, op_id)
    async with store.transaction():  # logged once; a resumed or repeated run finds it and writes nothing
        if not await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (run.undo_id,)):
            await log_op(store, run.undo_id, "undo", HUMAN, {"undo_of": op_id})
    await run.run()
    return await build_report(store, op_id)


class UndoRun:
    def __init__(self, store: Store, op_id: str) -> None:
        self.store = store
        self.op_id = op_id
        self.undo_id = f"undo:{op_id}"  # written next to every outcome this run decides

    async def run(self) -> None:
        await self._decide_rows(self.op_id, retrying_for=None)
        await self.retry_waiting()

    async def retry_waiting(self) -> None:
        """Rows of earlier undos that were skipped because this delete held a node they need.

        A row can only be blocked by its own journal or a newer one (everything it needs was live when its
        delete ran), so newer journals go first, and inside a journal nodes parents first, then arrows.
        """
        journals = await self.store.fetchall(
            """
            SELECT w.delete_op FROM (
                SELECT delete_op FROM removed_nodes WHERE outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?1
                UNION
                SELECT delete_op FROM removed_edges WHERE outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?1
            ) w JOIN ops o ON o.op_id = w.delete_op
            ORDER BY o.seq DESC
            """,
            (self.op_id,),
        )
        for (delete_op,) in journals:
            await self._decide_rows(delete_op, retrying_for=self.op_id)

    async def _decide_rows(self, delete_op: str, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
        """The pending rows of one journal: nodes parents first, then arrows, one step each."""
        if retrying_for is None:
            where, params = "outcome IS NULL", (delete_op,)
        else:
            where, params = "outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?", (delete_op, retrying_for)
        nodes = await self.store.fetchall(
            f"SELECT id FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND {where} ORDER BY ord", params
        )
        for (node_id,) in nodes:
            await self.node_step(delete_op, node_id, retrying_for)
        edges = await self.store.fetchall(
            f"SELECT from_id, to_id, type FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? AND {where} ORDER BY ord", params
        )
        for from_id, to_id, edge_type in edges:
            await self.edge_step(delete_op, (from_id, to_id, edge_type), retrying_for)

    # ---- steps -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def node_step(self, delete_op: str, node_id: str, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
        """One removed node and the arrow from its parent, in one transaction."""
        store = self.store
        async with store.transaction():
            row = await self._node_row(delete_op, node_id)
            if row is None or not _pending(row.outcome, row.waiting_on, retrying_for):
                return
            parent_arrow = (row.parent_id, row.id, CONTAINS) if row.parent_id is not None else None
            holder = await store.fetchval("SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE qualified_name = ?", (row.qualified_name,))
            if holder is not None:
                detail, prior = await self._merge_into(row, holder)
                await self._mark_node(row, MERGED, "name_in_use", merged_into=holder, detail=detail, prior=prior)
                target = holder
            else:
                if parent_arrow is not None:
                    parent = await self.where(parent_arrow[0])
                    if parent.live_id is None:
                        await self._mark_node(row, SKIPPED, "parent_not_live", waiting_on=parent.waiting_on)
                        await self._mark_edge(
                            delete_op, parent_arrow, SKIPPED, "endpoint_not_live", waiting_on=parent.waiting_on
                        )
                        return
                await store.write(
                    "INSERT INTO nodes (id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, effective_tags) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, '[]')",
                    (row.id, row.qualified_name, row.type, row.description, row.owner, row.tags),
                )
                await self._mark_node(row, RESTORED)
                target = row.id
            if parent_arrow is not None and await self._edge_pending(delete_op, parent_arrow, retrying_for):
                await self._decide_edge(delete_op, parent_arrow)
            # Recompute what this step can have changed: the node and everything now below it.
            await refresh_subtree(store, target)

    async def edge_step(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
        """One removed arrow, in one transaction."""
        async with self.store.transaction():
            if not await self._edge_pending(delete_op, edge, retrying_for):
                return
            added = await self._decide_edge(delete_op, edge)
            if added is not None and edge[2] == CONTAINS:
                await refresh_subtree(self.store, added[1])

    # ---- decisions ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def where(self, node_id: str) -> Place:
        """The live node that stands for node_id now, or the delete that has to be undone first.

        Follows merges (a merged id lives on as the node it was folded into). A node only disappears through
        a delete, so a node that is not live is always held by some journal row.
        """
        current = node_id
        seen: set[str] = set()
        while current not in seen:
            seen.add(current)
            if await node_live(self.store, current):
                return Place(current)
            rows = await self.store.fetchall(
                "SELECT r.outcome, r.merged_into, r.waiting_on, r.delete_op "
                "FROM removed_nodes r JOIN ops o ON o.op_id = r.delete_op WHERE r.id = ? ORDER BY o.seq DESC",
                (current,),
            )
            merged = next((r for r in rows if r[0] == MERGED), None)
            if merged is not None:
                current = merged[1]
                continue
            holder = next((r for r in rows if r[0] is None or r[0] == SKIPPED), None)
            if holder is None:
                return Place(None)
            outcome, _, waiting_on, delete_op = holder
            # Held by a delete nobody has undone yet, or by a row that is itself waiting on another delete.
            return Place(None, delete_op if outcome is None else waiting_on)
        return Place(None)

    async def _decide_edge(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
        """Decide one removed arrow and write the outcome. Returns the arrow added, if one was."""
        store = self.store
        from_id, to_id, edge_type = edge
        ends = (await self.where(from_id), await self.where(to_id))
        if any(end.live_id is None for end in ends):
            waiting_on = next((end.waiting_on for end in ends if end.live_id is None and end.waiting_on), None)
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "endpoint_not_live", waiting_on=waiting_on)
            return None
        now = (ends[0].live_id, ends[1].live_id)
        assert now[0] is not None and now[1] is not None
        if await edge_live(store, now[0], now[1], edge_type):
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, MERGED, "already_present", now=now)
            return None
        if edge_type == CONTAINS and await has_parent(store, now[1]):
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "child_has_other_parent", now=now)
            return None
        if await store.fetchval(
            "SELECT 1 FROM edge_removals WHERE from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ? AND actor = 'human' "
            "AND seq > (SELECT seq FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?) LIMIT 1",
            (*now, edge_type, delete_op),
        ):
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "removed_by_person", now=now)
            return None
        if edge_type == CONTAINS and await ancestor_or_self(store, now[1], now[0]):
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "would_create_cycle", now=now)
            return None
        await insert_edge(store, now[0], now[1], edge_type)
        if now == (from_id, to_id):
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, RESTORED)
        else:
            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, MERGED, "endpoint_merged", now=now)
        return now

    async def _merge_into(self, row: NodeRow, holder: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
        """Fold a removed node into the live node that holds its name.

        Returns the report detail, and `prior`: for every field whose value or write record changes, what the
        live node held before ({"value": ..., "write": [seq, actor] or null}), so a redo can put it back.
        """
        store = self.store
        live = await store.fetchone("SELECT type, description, owner, tags FROM nodes WHERE id = ?", (holder,))
        assert live is not None
        live_values = {"type": live[0], "description": live[1], "owner": live[2], "tags": json.loads(live[3])}
        old_values = {
            "type": row.type,
            "description": row.description,
            "owner": row.owner,
            "tags": json.loads(row.tags),
        }
        live_writes = {
            field: (seq, actor)
            for field, seq, actor in await store.fetchall(
                "SELECT field, seq, actor FROM field_writes WHERE node_id = ?", (holder,)
            )
        }
        old_writes = {field: (seq, actor) for field, (seq, actor) in json.loads(row.writes).items()}

        filled: list[str] = []
        kept_live: list[str] = []
        not_restored: dict[str, Any] = {}
        take_value: list[str] = []
        take_write: list[str] = []
        for field in WRITTEN_FIELDS:
            old_w, live_w = old_writes.get(field), live_writes.get(field)
            old_is_newer = old_w is not None and (live_w is None or old_w[0] > live_w[0])
            differs = old_values[field] != live_values[field]
            if field == "type" and not differs:
                # Same type either way: nothing to report. Keep the newest report time for later merges.
                if old_is_newer:
                    take_write.append(field)
                continue
            if old_is_newer:
                filled.append(field)
                take_value.append(field)
                take_write.append(field)
            else:
                kept_live.append(field)
                if old_w is not None and differs:
                    not_restored[field] = old_values[field]

        prior = {
            field: {"value": live_values[field], "write": list(live_writes[field]) if field in live_writes else None}
            for field in take_write
        }
        # A filled field that overwrote a value someone had written on the live node: show what was there.
        replaced = {
            field: live_values[field]
            for field in take_value
            if field in live_writes and live_values[field] != old_values[field]
        }
        if take_value:
            assignments = ", ".join(f"{field} = ?" for field in take_value)
            params = [tags_json(old_values[f]) if f == "tags" else old_values[f] for f in take_value]
            await store.write(f"UPDATE nodes SET {assignments} WHERE id = ?", (*params, holder))
        for field in take_write:
            seq, actor = old_writes[field]
            await record_write(store, holder, field, seq, actor)
        detail: dict[str, Any] = {"filled": filled, "kept_live": kept_live, "not_restored": not_restored}
        if replaced:
            detail["replaced"] = replaced
        return detail, prior

    # ---- journal rows ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _node_row(self, delete_op: str, node_id: str) -> NodeRow | None:
        row = await self.store.fetchone(NODE_ROW_SQL, (delete_op, node_id))
        return None if row is None else NodeRow(*row)

    async def _edge_pending(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge, retrying_for: str | None) -> bool:
        row = await self.store.fetchone(
            "SELECT outcome, waiting_on FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? AND from_id = ? AND to_id = ? "
            "AND type = ?",
            (delete_op, *edge),
        )
        return row is not None and _pending(row[0], row[1], retrying_for)

    async def _mark_node(
        self,
        row: NodeRow,
        outcome: str,
        reason: str | None = None,
        *,
        merged_into: str | None = None,
        waiting_on: str | None = None,
        detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        prior: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        await self.store.write(
            "UPDATE removed_nodes SET outcome = ?, reason = ?, merged_into = ?, waiting_on = ?, detail = ?, "
            "decided_by = ?, prior = ? WHERE delete_op = ? AND id = ?",
            (
                outcome,
                reason,
                merged_into,
                waiting_on,
                None if detail is None else json.dumps(detail, ensure_ascii=False),
                self.undo_id,
                None if prior is None else json.dumps(prior, ensure_ascii=False),
                row.delete_op,
                row.id,
            ),
        )

    async def _mark_edge(
        self,
        delete_op: str,
        edge: Edge,
        outcome: str,
        reason: str | None = None,
        *,
        now: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
        waiting_on: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        await self.store.write(
            "UPDATE removed_edges SET outcome = ?, reason = ?, waiting_on = ?, now_from = ?, now_to = ?, decided_by = ? "
            "WHERE delete_op = ? AND from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ?",
            (outcome, reason, waiting_on, *(now or (None, None)), self.undo_id, delete_op, *edge),
        )


# ---- report --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def build_report(store: Store, op_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The report is a printout of the delete's journal rows: one entry per removed node and arrow."""
    node_rows = await store.fetchall(
        "SELECT id, qualified_name, outcome, reason, merged_into, waiting_on, detail "
        "FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? ORDER BY ord",
        (op_id,),
    )
    edge_rows = await store.fetchall(
        "SELECT from_id, to_id, type, outcome, reason, waiting_on, now_from, now_to "
        "FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? ORDER BY ord",
        (op_id,),
    )
    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for node_id, name, outcome, reason, merged_into, waiting_on, detail in node_rows:
        entry: dict[str, Any] = {"id": node_id, "qualified_name": name, "outcome": outcome}
        if reason is not None:
            entry["reason"] = reason
        if merged_into is not None:
            entry["merged_into"] = merged_into
        if detail is not None:
            entry.update(json.loads(detail))
        if waiting_on is not None:
            entry["waiting_on"] = waiting_on
        nodes.append(entry)
    edges: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for from_id, to_id, edge_type, outcome, reason, waiting_on, now_from, now_to in edge_rows:
        entry = {"from": from_id, "to": to_id, "type": edge_type, "outcome": outcome}
        if reason is not None:
            entry["reason"] = reason
        if now_from is not None and outcome != RESTORED:
            entry["now"] = [now_from, now_to]
        if waiting_on is not None:
            entry["waiting_on"] = waiting_on
        edges.append(entry)
    summary = {"nodes": _count(nodes), "edges": _count(edges)}
    return {"op_id": op_id, "summary": summary, "nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}


def _count(entries: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, int]:
    counts = {RESTORED: 0, MERGED: 0, SKIPPED: 0}
    for entry in entries:
        counts[entry["outcome"]] += 1
    return counts


def format_report(report: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """JSON with one node or arrow per line, so the report reads like a table and diffs cleanly."""

    def block(key: str) -> str:
        items = report[key]
        if not items:
            return f'  "{key}": []'
        body = ",\n".join("    " + json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False) for item in items)
        return f'  "{key}": [\n{body}\n  ]'

    head = [
        f'  "op_id": {json.dumps(report["op_id"])}',
        f'  "summary": {json.dumps(report["summary"])}',
    ]
    return "{\n" + ",\n".join(head + [block("nodes"), block("edges")]) + "\n}\n"

3	SCHEMA = """
4	-- The live graph. dump prints these two tables and nothing else.
5	CREATE TABLE nodes (
6	    id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
7	    qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- the table holds live nodes only: a name is unique among live nodes
8	    type           TEXT NOT NULL,
9	    description    TEXT,
10	    owner          TEXT,
11	    tags           TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON list, set by people, in the order written
12	    effective_tags TEXT NOT NULL           -- JSON list, worked out, sorted
13	);

1	"""apply: run ops.jsonl in order, one transaction per operation.
2	
3	Five kinds of operation, each carrying an actor (human or ingest):
4	
5	    edit_node       human           set description, owner and/or tags of one live node
6	    add_edge        human, ingest   add a contains or references arrow between two live nodes
7	    repoint_edge    human, ingest   move one end of a live arrow (new_from_id or new_to_id); counts as one
8	                                    arrow taken away (kept in edge_removals) and one added
9	    ingest_node     ingest          by qualified_name: update the type of the live node that has the name,
10	                                    or create a node with an id built from op_id and name, under its parent
11	                                    when that parent is live; never sets description, owner or tags
12	    delete_subtree  human, ingest   remove a node, everything it contains and every arrow touching them;
13	                                    all of it moves into the journal under the delete's op_id
14	
15	Who did an operation matters in two places only. Ingest never sets description, owner or tags, so an
16	edit_node from ingest is refused. People do not create nodes or set types, so an ingest_node from a person
17	is refused.
18	
19	An operation that cannot be applied as written (it names a node or arrow that is not live, it would give a
20	node a second parent or make a node its own ancestor, a field has the wrong shape, ...) is stored as
21	rejected, with the reason, and changes nothing. A loop never gets into the graph.
22	
23	An op_id names one operation. One already in the database is skipped when the line is that same operation,
24	so running apply again on the same file is harmless. If it was used for a different operation, apply stops
25	with an error before it changes anything.
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	import json
31	import uuid
32	from collections import defaultdict
33	from pathlib import Path

39	    edge_live,

52	# ids on every run and the fixture generator can refer to ingested nodes in later operations.
53	INGEST_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("2f0c9a52-8a4e-4c55-9d1b-1b0f6d1e7a3c")
54

57	    return str(uuid.uuid5(INGEST_NAMESPACE, f"{op_id}/{qualified_name}"))

60	class Rejected(Exception):
61	    def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None:
62	        super().__init__(reason)
63	        self.reason = reason

65

67	    value = op.get(key)

80	class Applier:
81	    def __init__(self, store: Store) -> None:
82	        self.store = store
83	        self._handlers = {
84	            "edit_node": self._edit_node,
85	            "add_edge": self._add_edge,

92	        records = await read_jsonl(path)
93	        seen: set[str] = set()
94	        for lineno, op in records:
95	            op_id = op.get("op_id")
96	            if not isinstance(op_id, str) or not op_id:
97	                raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: op_id must be a non-empty string")
98	            if op_id in seen:

104	                raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: op_id {op['op_id']} was already applied as a different operation")

113	    async def apply_one(self, op: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
114	        store = self.store
115	        op_id = op["op_id"]
116	        async with store.transaction():
117	            if await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (op_id,)):
118	                return "already_applied", None
119	            kind, actor = op.get("kind"), op.get("actor")
120	            seq = await log_op(store, op_id, str(kind), str(actor), op)
121	            await store.control("SAVEPOINT op_body")
122	            try:

125	                handler = self._handlers.get(kind) if isinstance(kind, str) else None
126	                if handler is None:
127	                    raise Rejected("unknown_kind")
128	                await handler(op, seq, actor)
129	            except Rejected as rejected:

131	                await store.control("RELEASE op_body")
132	                await store.write(
133	                    "UPDATE ops SET status = 'rejected', reason = ? WHERE seq = ?", (rejected.reason, seq)
134	                )
135	                return "rejected", rejected.reason
136	            await store.control("RELEASE op_body")
137	        return "applied", None

139	    async def _check_new_arrow(self, from_id: str, to_id: str, edge_type: str, *, child_moves: bool = False) -> None:
140	        """Refuse an arrow that exists already, or a contains arrow that would give its child a second
141	        parent (unless the child is moving away from its current one) or make a node its own ancestor."""
142	        if await edge_live(self.store, from_id, to_id, edge_type):
143	            raise Rejected("edge_exists")
144	        if edge_type == CONTAINS:

146	                raise Rejected("child_has_parent")

174	        if not (await node_live(self.store, from_id) and await node_live(self.store, to_id)):

182	        from_id, to_id, edge_type = _text(op, "from_id"), _text(op, "to_id"), _edge_type(op)

    repoint_edge    human, ingest   move one end of a live arrow (new_from_id or new_to_id); counts as one
                                    arrow taken away (kept in edge_removals) and one added
    ingest_node     ingest          by qualified_name: update the type of the live node that has the name,
                                    or create a node with an id built from op_id and name, under its parent
                                    when that parent is live; never sets description, owner or tags
    delete_subtree  human, ingest   remove a node, everything it contains and every arrow touching them;
                                    all of it moves into the journal under the delete's op_id

Who did an operation matters in two places only. Ingest never sets description, owner or tags, so an
edit_node from ingest is refused. People do not create nodes or set types, so an ingest_node from a person
is refused.

An operation that cannot be applied as written (it names a node or arrow that is not live, it would give a
node a second parent or make a node its own ancestor, a field has the wrong shape, ...) is stored as
rejected, with the reason, and changes nothing. A loop never gets into the graph.

An op_id names one operation. One already in the database is skipped when the line is that same operation,
so running apply again on the same file is harmless. If it was used for a different operation, apply stops
with an error before it changes anything.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .common import ACTORS, AUTHORED, CONTAINS, EDGE_TYPES, HUMAN, INGEST, InputError, read_jsonl, tags_json, valid_value
from .graph import (
    ancestor_or_self,
    edge_live,
    has_parent,
    insert_edge,
    log_op,
    node_live,
    record_write,
    subtree,
    walk_down,
)
from .store import Store
from .tags import refresh_all, refresh_subtree

# An ingest that creates a node builds the id from the op_id and the name, so the same files give the same
# ids on every run and the fixture generator can refer to ingested nodes in later operations.
INGEST_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("2f0c9a52-8a4e-4c55-9d1b-1b0f6d1e7a3c")


def ingest_node_id(op_id: str, qualified_name: str) -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid5(INGEST_NAMESPACE, f"{op_id}/{qualified_name}"))


class Rejected(Exception):
    def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(reason)
        self.reason = reason


def _text(op: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> str:
    value = op.get(key)
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        raise Rejected("malformed")
    return value


def _edge_type(op: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    value = op.get("type")
    if value not in EDGE_TYPES:
        raise Rejected("malformed")
    return value


class Applier:
    def __init__(self, store: Store) -> None:
        self.store = store
        self._handlers = {
            "edit_node": self._edit_node,
            "add_edge": self._add_edge,
            "repoint_edge": self._repoint_edge,
            "ingest_node": self._ingest_node,
            "delete_subtree": self._delete_subtree,
        }

    async def apply_file(self, path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
        records = await read_jsonl(path)
        seen: set[str] = set()
        for lineno, op in records:
            op_id = op.get("op_id")
            if not isinstance(op_id, str) or not op_id:
                raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: op_id must be a non-empty string")
            if op_id in seen:
                raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: op_id {op_id} appears twice")
            seen.add(op_id)
        for lineno, op in records:
            stored = await self.store.fetchval("SELECT payload FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (op["op_id"],))
            if stored is not None and json.loads(stored) != op:
                raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: op_id {op['op_id']} was already applied as a different operation")
        summary: dict[str, Any] = {"applied": 0, "rejected": 0, "already_applied": 0, "rejections": {}}
        for _, op in records:
            status, reason = await self.apply_one(op)
            summary[status] += 1
            if status == "rejected":
                summary["rejections"][op["op_id"]] = reason
        return summary

    async def apply_one(self, op: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
        store = self.store
        op_id = op["op_id"]
        async with store.transaction():
            if await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?", (op_id,)):
                return "already_applied", None
            kind, actor = op.get("kind"), op.get("actor")
            seq = await log_op(store, op_id, str(kind), str(actor), op)
            await store.control("SAVEPOINT op_body")
            try:
                if actor not in ACTORS:
                    raise Rejected("unknown_actor")
                handler = self._handlers.get(kind) if isinstance(kind, str) else None
                if handler is None:
                    raise Rejected("unknown_kind")
                await handler(op, seq, actor)
            except Rejected as rejected:
                await store.control("ROLLBACK TO op_body")
                await store.control("RELEASE op_body")
                await store.write(
                    "UPDATE ops SET status = 'rejected', reason = ? WHERE seq = ?", (rejected.reason, seq)
                )
                return "rejected", rejected.reason
            await store.control("RELEASE op_body")
        return "applied", None

    async def _check_new_arrow(self, from_id: str, to_id: str, edge_type: str, *, child_moves: bool = False) -> None:
        """Refuse an arrow that exists already, or a contains arrow that would give its child a second
        parent (unless the child is moving away from its current one) or make a node its own ancestor."""
        if await edge_live(self.store, from_id, to_id, edge_type):
            raise Rejected("edge_exists")
        if edge_type == CONTAINS:
            if not child_moves and await has_parent(self.store, to_id):
                raise Rejected("child_has_parent")
            if await ancestor_or_self(self.store, to_id, from_id):
                raise Rejected("would_create_cycle")

    # ---- the five kinds ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _edit_node(self, op: dict[str, Any], seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
        if actor != HUMAN:
            raise Rejected("actor_not_allowed")
        node_id = _text(op, "id")
        changes = op.get("set")
        if not isinstance(changes, dict) or not changes:
            raise Rejected("malformed")
        if any(field not in AUTHORED or not valid_value(field, value) for field, value in changes.items()):
            raise Rejected("malformed")
        if not await node_live(self.store, node_id):
            raise Rejected("node_not_live")
        fields = sorted(changes)
        assignments = ", ".join(f"{field} = ?" for field in fields)
        params = [tags_json(changes[f]) if f == "tags" else changes[f] for f in fields]
        await self.store.write(f"UPDATE nodes SET {assignments} WHERE id = ?", (*params, node_id))
        for field in fields:
            await record_write(self.store, node_id, field, seq, actor)
        if "tags" in changes:
            await refresh_subtree(self.store, node_id)

    async def _add_edge(self, op: dict[str, Any], seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
        from_id, to_id, edge_type = _text(op, "from_id"), _text(op, "to_id"), _edge_type(op)
        if not (await node_live(self.store, from_id) and await node_live(self.store, to_id)):
            raise Rejected("endpoint_not_live")
        await self._check_new_arrow(from_id, to_id, edge_type)
        await insert_edge(self.store, from_id, to_id, edge_type)
        if edge_type == CONTAINS:
            await refresh_subtree(self.store, to_id)

    async def _repoint_edge(self, op: dict[str, Any], seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
        from_id, to_id, edge_type = _text(op, "from_id"), _text(op, "to_id"), _edge_type(op)
        has_new_from, has_new_to = op.get("new_from_id") is not None, op.get("new_to_id") is not None
        if has_new_from == has_new_to:
            raise Rejected("malformed")  # exactly one end moves
        moved = _text(op, "new_from_id" if has_new_from else "new_to_id")
        new_from, new_to = (moved, to_id) if has_new_from else (from_id, moved)
        if not await edge_live(self.store, from_id, to_id, edge_type):
            raise Rejected("edge_not_live")
        if not await node_live(self.store, moved):
            raise Rejected("endpoint_not_live")
        await self._check_new_arrow(new_from, new_to, edge_type, child_moves=has_new_from)
        await self.store.write(
            "DELETE FROM edges WHERE from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ?", (from_id, to_id, edge_type)
        )
        await insert_edge(self.store, new_from, new_to, edge_type)
        await self.store.write(
            "INSERT INTO edge_removals (from_id, to_id, type, seq, actor, op_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (from_id, to_id, edge_type, seq, actor, op["op_id"]),
        )
        if edge_type == CONTAINS:
            await refresh_subtree(self.store, to_id)  # moved under a new parent, or lost its parent
            if new_to != to_id:
                await refresh_subtree(self.store, new_to)

    async def _ingest_node(self, op: dict[str, Any], seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
        if actor != INGEST:
            raise Rejected("actor_not_allowed")
        if any(field in op for field in AUTHORED):
            raise Rejected("ingest_sets_authored_field")
        name, node_type = _text(op, "qualified_name"), _text(op, "type")
        parent_name = op.get("parent")
        if parent_name is not None and not isinstance(parent_name, str):
            raise Rejected("malformed")
        holder = await self.store.fetchone("SELECT id, type FROM nodes WHERE qualified_name = ?", (name,))
        if holder is not None:
            holder_id, holder_type = holder
            if holder_type != node_type:
                await self.store.write("UPDATE nodes SET type = ? WHERE id = ?", (node_type, holder_id))
            await record_write(self.store, holder_id, "type", seq, actor)  # the most recent report of the type
            return
        node_id = ingest_node_id(op["op_id"], name)
        parent_id = None
        if parent_name:
            parent_id = await self.store.fetchval("SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE qualified_name = ?", (parent_name,))
        await self.store.write(
            "INSERT INTO nodes (id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, effective_tags) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, '[]', '[]')",
            (node_id, name, node_type),
        )
        await record_write(self.store, node_id, "type", seq, actor)
        if parent_id is not None:
            await insert_edge(self.store, parent_id, node_id, CONTAINS)
            await refresh_subtree(self.store, node_id)

    async def _delete_subtree(self, op: dict[str, Any], seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
        root = _text(op, "root_id")
        if not await node_live(self.store, root):
            raise Rejected("node_not_live")
        store = self.store
        rows, children = await subtree(store, root)
        by_id = {row.id: row for row in rows}
        order = [node for node, _ in walk_down([root], children)]  # parents first

        await store.control("CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS doomed (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY)")
        await store.write("DELETE FROM temp.doomed")
        await store.write_many("INSERT INTO temp.doomed (id) VALUES (?)", [(node_id,) for node_id in order])
        touching = await store.fetchall(
            "SELECT from_id, to_id, type FROM edges "
            "WHERE from_id IN (SELECT id FROM temp.doomed) OR to_id IN (SELECT id FROM temp.doomed)"
        )
        writes: dict[str, dict[str, list[Any]]] = defaultdict(dict)
        for node_id, field, write_seq, write_actor in await store.fetchall(
            "SELECT node_id, field, seq, actor FROM field_writes WHERE node_id IN (SELECT id FROM temp.doomed)"
        ):
            writes[node_id][field] = [write_seq, write_actor]

        await store.write_many(
            "INSERT INTO removed_nodes (delete_op, ord, id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, "
            "parent_id, writes) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            [
                (
                    op["op_id"],
                    ord_,
                    node_id,
                    by_id[node_id].qualified_name,
                    by_id[node_id].type,
                    by_id[node_id].description,
                    by_id[node_id].owner,
                    by_id[node_id].tags,
                    by_id[node_id].parent_id,
                    json.dumps(writes.get(node_id, {}), sort_keys=True),
                )
                for ord_, node_id in enumerate(order)
            ],
        )
        # Every contains arrow touching the subtree ends inside it: it is the arrow from a node's parent.
        rank = {node_id: i for i, node_id in enumerate(order)}
        parent_arrows = sorted((e for e in touching if e[2] == CONTAINS), key=lambda e: rank[e[1]])
        other_arrows = sorted(e for e in touching if e[2] != CONTAINS)
        await store.write_many(
            "INSERT INTO removed_edges (delete_op, ord, from_id, to_id, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            [(op["op_id"], i, *edge) for i, edge in enumerate(parent_arrows + other_arrows)],
        )
        # Arrows first, then nodes: the database refuses a node that an arrow still points at.
        await store.write(
            "DELETE FROM edges WHERE from_id IN (SELECT id FROM temp.doomed) OR to_id IN (SELECT id FROM temp.doomed)"
        )
        await store.write("DELETE FROM nodes WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM temp.doomed)")
        await store.write("DELETE FROM temp.doomed")
        # Recompute effective_tags of the remaining nodes. In a tree no value changes (a node that inherited
        # from the subtree was inside it), so this writes nothing; it keeps the stored values honest anyway.
        await refresh_all(store)

"""Reads and writes that apply, undo and the tag propagator share: the live graph and the operation log."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import defaultdict, deque
from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
from typing import Any, NamedTuple

from .common import utc_now
from .store import Store

# A node and everything below it along contains arrows, each with its contains parent. UNION (not
# UNION ALL) drops a node it has already found, so the walk ends even if a contains loop ever existed.
SUBTREE_SQL = """
WITH RECURSIVE sub(id) AS (
    SELECT ?
    UNION
    SELECT e.to_id FROM edges e JOIN sub ON e.from_id = sub.id WHERE e.type = 'contains'
)
SELECT n.id, n.qualified_name, n.type, n.description, n.owner, n.tags, n.effective_tags,
       (SELECT p.from_id FROM edges p WHERE p.to_id = n.id AND p.type = 'contains')
FROM sub JOIN nodes n ON n.id = sub.id
"""

# Walk up from the second id along contains arrows; 1 when the first id is on the way (or is the second).
ANCESTOR_OR_SELF_SQL = """
WITH RECURSIVE up(id) AS (
    SELECT ?2
    UNION
    SELECT e.from_id FROM edges e JOIN up ON e.to_id = up.id WHERE e.type = 'contains'
)
SELECT 1 FROM up WHERE id = ?1 LIMIT 1
"""


class SubtreeRow(NamedTuple):
    id: str
    qualified_name: str
    type: str
    description: str | None
    owner: str | None
    tags: str
    effective_tags: str
    parent_id: str | None


def walk_down(roots: Iterable[str], children: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """Every node below the roots once, parents before children, as (node, parent). Siblings in id order."""
    queue: deque[tuple[str, str | None]] = deque((root, None) for root in roots)
    seen: set[str] = set()
    while queue:
        node, parent = queue.popleft()
        if node in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(node)
        yield node, parent
        queue.extend((child, node) for child in sorted(children.get(node, ())))


async def subtree(store: Store, root: str) -> tuple[list[SubtreeRow], dict[str, list[str]]]:
    """The rows of root and everything below it, and the children of each of them."""
    rows = [SubtreeRow(*row) for row in await store.fetchall(SUBTREE_SQL, (root,))]
    children: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        if row.id != root and row.parent_id is not None:
            children[row.parent_id].append(row.id)
    return rows, children


async def node_live(store: Store, node_id: str) -> bool:
    return bool(await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM nodes WHERE id = ?", (node_id,)))


async def edge_live(store: Store, from_id: str, to_id: str, edge_type: str) -> bool:
    return bool(
        await store.fetchval(
            "SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ?", (from_id, to_id, edge_type)
        )
    )


async def has_parent(store: Store, node_id: str) -> bool:
    return bool(await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE to_id = ? AND type = 'contains'", (node_id,)))


async def ancestor_or_self(store: Store, ancestor: str, node_id: str) -> bool:
    """True when ancestor is node_id itself or above it along contains arrows."""
    return bool(await store.fetchval(ANCESTOR_OR_SELF_SQL, (ancestor, node_id)))


async def insert_edge(store: Store, from_id: str, to_id: str, edge_type: str) -> None:
    await store.write("INSERT INTO edges (from_id, to_id, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (from_id, to_id, edge_type))


async def log_op(store: Store, op_id: str, kind: str, actor: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    """Add an operation to the log with the next running number, and return that number."""
    seq = await store.fetchval("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM ops")
    await store.write(
        "INSERT INTO ops (seq, op_id, kind, actor, applied_at, status, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'applied', ?)",
        (seq, op_id, kind, actor, utc_now(), json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)),
    )
    return seq


async def record_write(store: Store, node_id: str, field: str, seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
    """Remember who wrote this field of this node last, and in which operation."""
    await store.write(
        "INSERT INTO field_writes (node_id, field, seq, actor) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
        "ON CONFLICT (node_id, field) DO UPDATE SET seq = excluded.seq, actor = excluded.actor",
        (node_id, field, seq, actor),
    )

The redo design fits what the task implies, but it has four gaps that would produce wrong results once built. I changed nothing and ran nothing: redo isn't implemented, so this comes from reading the PDF, the new design and the undo code.

**What holds up**
- Redo is the inverse of the undo applied to the current graph, which mirrors the task's wording for undo.
- Nothing a person did after the undo is lost; this is the analogue of invariant 1.
- One row per transaction, children first, with foreign keys on, so a dump between crashed runs stays whole (invariant 7).
- The example redo report agrees row for row with the example undo report.
- The undo code already stores what redo needs for the simple case: `decided_by`, `prior`, and `now_from`/`now_to`.

**Gaps that give wrong results**

1. **Rows undo skipped are not reopened.** The design only says a row "has no outcome again" for removed nodes; skipped rows are "nothing to take back".
   - Example ("The parent is deleted later"): undo d1 skips everything waiting on d2, then redo d1, then undo d2. `retry_waiting` in [undo.py:124](graph_undo/undo.py:124) still finds those rows and restores `sales.orders`, although d1 was redone.
   - The same staleness breaks invariant 2 for a second undo: a row left as "merged into n8" is never reconsidered if n8 is deleted later.
   - Fix: after redo, every row is either kept (still live) or fully open, with no outcome and no `waiting_on`.

2. **Rounds are underspecified.**
   - The design doesn't say how `undo d1` tells a repeat run (invariant 6) from a new round after a redo; [undo.py:118](graph_undo/undo.py:118) hardcodes `undo:<op_id>`.
   - Redo outcomes from round 1 stay on the rows, so round 2's "skip rows that already have a redo outcome" would skip everything.
   - Nothing covers a redo started on a half-finished undo, or the reverse.
   - `undo:d1:2` is ambiguous with a delete whose op_id is `d1:2`.

3. **With two deletes, "rows this undo decided" gives a surprising result.** After undo d1 then undo d2 in the parent story, every d1 row carries `decided_by = undo:d2`. So `redo d1` has nothing to take back, and `sales.orders` can only leave by redoing d2, which also removes `sales`. The redo stories cover only the neighbour case. Either let redo d1 cover all of d1's own rows whoever decided them, or state this behaviour and add the story.

4. **There is no redo counterpart to "a later delete is in the way".** The design has no outcome for:
   - a restored node that a newer delete removed again before the redo;
   - a merge target that is no longer live;
   - a node restored by one undo that another undo then merged fields into. It is only kept today if it happens to have children, so a leaf would be removed carrying the other undo's fields.

**Smaller points**
- **Arrow precedence:** an arrow with one removed end and one kept end matches both "removed" and "kept, `end_kept`". It has to be removed, so state the order as undo does.
- **Checker:** there is no analogue of invariant 2. A redo that keeps too much passes every listed check except the straight-after-undo one.
- **`edge_removals`:** redo's arrow removals must not be recorded there, or the next undo skips them as `removed_by_person`.
- **Wording:** section 3 still says "Only undo reads the variable" for `CRASH_AFTER`. "A person has written the field" should also cover `type` written by ingest.
- **Repo:** [docs/design.html](docs/design.html) is still the version without section 4, and the README and DECISIONS.md describe four commands. DECISIONS.md must stay one page.
- **Sessions:** this session counts as an AI session to export for the submission.

Should I write the fixes for points 1–4 into the design page, or would you rather pick which ones?

content.text:
All four use the six-node example: `sales` contains `sales.orders` and `sales.refunds`, `sales.orders` contains `email` and `total`, and `reports.daily` references `sales.orders` and `total`.

## 1. Redo leaves skipped rows waiting

**Situation** (your story "The parent is deleted later"):

1. d1 deletes `sales.orders` with `email` and `total`.
2. d2 deletes `sales`, which takes `sales.refunds` with it.
3. `undo d1`: the parent `sales` is not live, so every row of d1 is skipped with `waiting_on: d2`. The graph does not change.
4. `redo d1`: the person decides d1 should stand after all.
5. `undo d2`: `sales` and `sales.refunds` come back.

**Issue:** in step 4, redo finds no restored nodes, no merges and no added arrows, so by the design every row is "unchanged, nothing to take back". The rows stay skipped and still wait on d2. In step 5, undo d2 retries every row that waits on d2 ([undo.py:124](graph_undo/undo.py:124)) and restores `sales.orders`, `email`, `total` and their arrows. The person's last word on d1 was redo, yet d1's content is back.

A skipped row that waits is a promise to come back when the other delete is undone. Redo has to cancel that promise, and the design only resets rows for removed nodes.

**Same cause, second symptom** (your usual story):

1. `undo d1` merges old `email` (n3) into n8 with nothing filled.
2. `redo d1` reports n3 as "unchanged, nothing_filled", and the row still says "merged into n8".
3. Someone deletes n8.
4. `undo d1` again: only rows with no outcome are decided, so n3 is passed over.

The name `sales.orders.email` is free and its parent is live, so invariant 2 says n3 must be restored, and it is not. The report also lists a merge into a node that is not live, which your check 4 rejects.

**Fix:** one rule. After redo, every row the undo decided is either kept (still live, outcome stays) or open again, with no outcome and no `waiting_on`.

## 2. Rounds are not defined

A round is one undo plus its redo. The design names the second round `undo:d1:2` and `redo:d1:2`, but leaves three things open.

- **Repeat or new round.** `undo d1` run twice in a row must write nothing (invariant 6). `undo d1` after a redo must be a real undo. The design never says how the tool tells them apart, and the code always uses `undo:d1` ([undo.py:118](graph_undo/undo.py:118)). The rule needed: look at the newest undo or redo entry in `ops` for this delete. If it is the same command, this call repeats or resumes it. If it is the other command, a new round starts.

- **Old redo outcomes block the next redo.**
  1. Round 1: undo restores `total`, redo removes it. The row gets redo outcome "removed".
  2. Round 2: undo restores `total` again.
  3. `redo d1`: the design says a run skips every row that already has a redo outcome. `total` has one from round 1, so it is skipped and stays live.

  So "undo and redo can go back and forth" fails on the second redo. Either undo clears the redo outcome when it decides a row again, or each redo outcome carries its round and only this round's are skipped.

- **A crash, then the other command.** `CRASH_AFTER=5 undo d1` stops with half the nodes back, and the person runs `redo d1` instead of finishing. The design says only an undone delete can be redone, and does not say whether a half-undone one counts. The mirror case is a crashed redo followed by `undo d1`: a repeat would write nothing and leave the graph half redone. The simplest rule is that each command refuses while the other is unfinished. That needs a "finished" mark on the entry in `ops`, because today the entry is written when the undo starts.

A smaller point: an op_id can be any string, so `undo:d1:2` could also mean round 1 of a delete named `d1:2`. Keeping the delete and the round number as separate values avoids parsing the name.

## 3. Which rows a redo owns

**Situation** (the parent story again, both deletes undone):

1. d1 deletes `sales.orders`, d2 deletes `sales`.
2. `undo d1`: everything waits on d2.
3. `undo d2`: restores `sales`, then retries d1's rows and restores them. Each of those rows now records `decided_by: undo:d2`.
4. The person wants `sales.orders` gone again but `sales` kept, and runs `redo d1`.

**Issue:** redo takes "every row that the undo of this delete decided". No row is still marked as decided by undo d1, so `redo d1` does nothing. The only command that removes `sales.orders` is `redo d2`, which also removes `sales` and `sales.refunds`. The state "d2 undone, d1 redone" cannot be reached.

Had the undos run in the other order, d2 then d1, the same graph would result but d1's rows would belong to undo d1, and `redo d1` would work. The outcome depends on a past order the person cannot see.

The text also reads two ways. Step 1 says redo takes "the delete's own rows". The story "Or: redo d1" says an arrow that is d1's own row is not taken back, because undo d2 put it there.

**Two ways to settle it:**

- **By delete (my recommendation).** `redo d1` covers every row of d1 that is currently put back, whoever decided it, plus rows of other deletes that undo d1 retried. In the parent story it removes `sales.orders` and leaves `sales`. In "Or: redo d1" the two arrows from `reports.daily` go out with their nodes and nothing is kept, so that step of the story changes.
- **By decider (what the story shows).** Keep it, add the parent case as a story, and have `redo d1` say why it did nothing.

I prefer the first because the undo report already works that way: a retried row keeps its entry in the report of its own delete.

## 4. Later changes in the way: my opinions

- **A restored node was deleted again by a newer delete d3.** Redo should leave it alone: outcome `unchanged`, reason `deleted_since`, naming d3. The d1 row should be opened like any other. A later `undo d1` then restores the node from d1's copy, which invariant 2 requires since the name is free. A later `undo d3` merges its newer copy in by "most recent write wins". This merges a node into its own id, which the code looks able to handle, but it needs one test.

- **The merge target is no longer live.** Say n7 was deleted by d3 after undo filled its description. Redo should report `unchanged`, reason `target_not_live`, and open the row. I would not reach into d3's journal to take the filled value out, because a journal should stay a true copy of what its delete removed. The cost is that undoing d3 later brings n7 back with that description. That is acceptable as long as the report shows it.

- **One undo restored a node and another undo merged into it.** For example, undo d2 restores n7, undo d1 merges old n2 into it, then `redo d2` runs. n7 passes both tests, because the filled field carries its old write number and nothing is attached. It would be removed, carrying d1's restored description with it. I would keep it, reason `still_in_use`, whenever a standing merge from another undo points at it. This fits your "redo the newest undo first" rule: `redo d1` reverts the fill, then `redo d2` removes n7 cleanly.

Each of these needs a defined outcome, so the report covers every row once and redo never trips on a missing node. Given the time limit, I would add one small-fixture test for the first case, since deleting again is the likeliest, and one sentence each for the other two.

Which of these do you want written into the design page?

  • Independent. It touched something undo did not put back. Rule: left exactly as it is.
  • Conflicting. A person wrote on, or attached something to, a thing undo put back. Example: a person rewrote the description of the restored sales.orders.total. Rule: that thing stays, with everything it needs to stay whole: its parents and its arrows. The report lists it as kept.
  • Caused. It happened only because the undo happened. Example: the ingest found sales.orders.total live again and updated its type instead of creating a new node. Rule: it does not hold redo back, and the journal copy keeps the newer type.

Redo only takes back rows undo decided, and only while they are as undo left them. It never overwrites or removes anything a person did after the undo.

Redo, undo, and their order

  • Redo straight after undo gives back the graph from before the undo. Nothing has changed in between, so every row is taken back. The dump is the same, byte for byte, as the dump taken just before the undo.
  • Undo can run again after a redo. The rows redo took back have no outcome, so undo decides them like new rows. With nothing changed in between, it gives the same graph as the first undo.
  • Only an undone delete can be redone. For a delete that was never undone, for any other operation, or for an id that does not exist, redo prints an error and writes nothing.
  • After several undos, redo the newest undo first. If an older undo is redone while a newer one still stands, some of its nodes may carry arrows or children the newer undo put there. Those nodes are kept, reason still_in_use. Redone newest first, nothing is kept for this reason. This mirrors undo, where the newest delete undone first means nothing waits.
  • Each round has its own entry in ops. The first undo of d1 is undo:d1 and its redo is redo:d1. A second round is undo:d1:2 and redo:d1:2. Every row names the undo that decided it, so "since it came back" always has an exact meaning.

Crashes and running it twice

  • One row, one transaction, as for undo. The graph change, the tag refresh and the row's redo outcome are saved together or not at all.
  • Each journal row gets a redo outcome next to its undo outcome: removed, kept or unchanged for nodes and arrows, and reverted for a merged node, with a reason. The report is a printout of those.
  • Crash and resume. CRASH_AFTER=<n> works for redo as it does for undo. A resumed run skips every row that already has a redo outcome.
  • Run it twice. The second run finds a redo outcome on every row, writes nothing, and prints the same report.
