144	    async def _decide_rows(self, delete_op: str, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
145	        """The pending rows of one journal: nodes parents first, then arrows, one step each."""
146	        if retrying_for is None:
147	            where, params = "outcome IS NULL", (delete_op,)
148	        else:
149	            where, params = "outcome = 'skipped' AND waiting_on = ?", (delete_op, retrying_for)
150	        nodes = await self.store.fetchall(
151	            f"SELECT id FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND {where} ORDER BY ord", params
152	        )
153	        for (node_id,) in nodes:
154	            await self.node_step(delete_op, node_id, retrying_for)
155	        edges = await self.store.fetchall(
156	            f"SELECT from_id, to_id, type FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? AND {where} ORDER BY ord", params
157	        )
158	        for from_id, to_id, edge_type in edges:
159	            await self.edge_step(delete_op, (from_id, to_id, edge_type), retrying_for)
160	
161	    # ---- steps -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
162	
163	    async def node_step(self, delete_op: str, node_id: str, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
164	        """One removed node and the arrow from its parent, in one transaction."""
165	        store = self.store
166	        async with store.transaction():
167	            row = await self._node_row(delete_op, node_id)
168	            if row is None or not _pending(row.outcome, row.waiting_on, retrying_for):
169	                return
170	            parent_arrow = (row.parent_id, row.id, CONTAINS) if row.parent_id is not None else None
171	            holder = await store.fetchval("SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE qualified_name = ?", (row.qualified_name,))
172	            if holder is not None:
173	                detail, prior = await self._merge_into(row, holder)
174	                await self._mark_node(row, MERGED, "name_in_use", merged_into=holder, detail=detail, prior=prior)
175	                target = holder
176	            else:
177	                if parent_arrow is not None:
178	                    parent = await self.where(parent_arrow[0])
179	                    if parent.live_id is None:
180	                        await self._mark_node(row, SKIPPED, "parent_not_live", waiting_on=parent.waiting_on)
181	                        await self._mark_edge(
182	                            delete_op, parent_arrow, SKIPPED, "endpoint_not_live", waiting_on=parent.waiting_on
183	                        )
184	                        return
185	                await store.write(
186	                    "INSERT INTO nodes (id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, effective_tags) "
187	                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, '[]')",
188	                    (row.id, row.qualified_name, row.type, row.description, row.owner, row.tags),
189	                )
190	                await self._mark_node(row, RESTORED)
191	                target = row.id
192	            if parent_arrow is not None and await self._edge_pending(delete_op, parent_arrow, retrying_for):
193	                await self._decide_edge(delete_op, parent_arrow)
194	            # Recompute what this step can have changed: the node and everything now below it.
195	            await refresh_subtree(store, target)
196	
197	    async def edge_step(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge, retrying_for: str | None) -> None:
198	        """One removed arrow, in one transaction."""
199	        async with self.store.transaction():
200	            if not await self._edge_pending(delete_op, edge, retrying_for):
201	                return
202	            added = await self._decide_edge(delete_op, edge)
203	            if added is not None and edge[2] == CONTAINS:
204	                await refresh_subtree(self.store, added[1])
205	
206	    # ---- decisions ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    async def where(self, node_id: str) -> Place:
209	        """The live node that stands for node_id now, or the delete that has to be undone first.
210	
211	        Follows merges (a merged id lives on as the node it was folded into). A node only disappears through
212	        a delete, so a node that is not live is always held by some journal row.
213	        """
214	        current = node_id
215	        seen: set[str] = set()
216	        while current not in seen:
217	            seen.add(current)
218	            if await node_live(self.store, current):
219	                return Place(current)
220	            rows = await self.store.fetchall(
221	                "SELECT r.outcome, r.merged_into, r.waiting_on, r.delete_op "
222	                "FROM removed_nodes r JOIN ops o ON o.op_id = r.delete_op WHERE r.id = ? ORDER BY o.seq DESC",
223	                (current,),
224	            )
225	            merged = next((r for r in rows if r[0] == MERGED), None)
226	            if merged is not None:
227	                current = merged[1]
228	                continue
229	            holder = next((r for r in rows if r[0] is None or r[0] == SKIPPED), None)
230	            if holder is None:
231	                return Place(None)
232	            outcome, _, waiting_on, delete_op = holder
233	            # Held by a delete nobody has undone yet, or by a row that is itself waiting on another delete.
234	            return Place(None, delete_op if outcome is None else waiting_on)
235	        return Place(None)
236	
237	    async def _decide_edge(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
238	        """Decide one removed arrow and write the outcome. Returns the arrow added, if one was."""
239	        store = self.store
240	        from_id, to_id, edge_type = edge
241	        ends = (await self.where(from_id), await self.where(to_id))
242	        if any(end.live_id is None for end in ends):
243	            waiting_on = next((end.waiting_on for end in ends if end.live_id is None and end.waiting_on), None)
244	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "endpoint_not_live", waiting_on=waiting_on)
245	            return None
246	        now = (ends[0].live_id, ends[1].live_id)
247	        assert now[0] is not None and now[1] is not None
248	        if await edge_live(store, now[0], now[1], edge_type):
249	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, MERGED, "already_present", now=now)
250	            return None
251	        if edge_type == CONTAINS and await has_parent(store, now[1]):
252	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "child_has_other_parent", now=now)
253	            return None
254	        if await store.fetchval(
255	            "SELECT 1 FROM edge_removals WHERE from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ? AND actor = 'human' "
256	            "AND seq > (SELECT seq FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?) LIMIT 1",
257	            (*now, edge_type, delete_op),
258	        ):
259	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "removed_by_person", now=now)
260	            return None
261	        if edge_type == CONTAINS and await ancestor_or_self(store, now[1], now[0]):
262	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, SKIPPED, "would_create_cycle", now=now)
263	            return None
264	        await insert_edge(store, now[0], now[1], edge_type)
265	        if now == (from_id, to_id):
266	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, RESTORED)
267	        else:
268	            await self._mark_edge(delete_op, edge, MERGED, "endpoint_merged", now=now)
269	        return now
270	
271	    async def _merge_into(self, row: NodeRow, holder: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
272	        """Fold a removed node into the live node that holds its name.
273	
274	        Returns the report detail, and `prior`: for every field whose value or write record changes, what the
275	        live node held before ({"value": ..., "write": [seq, actor] or null}), so a redo can put it back.
276	        """
277	        store = self.store
278	        live = await store.fetchone("SELECT type, description, owner, tags FROM nodes WHERE id = ?", (holder,))
279	        assert live is not None
280	        live_values = {"type": live[0], "description": live[1], "owner": live[2], "tags": json.loads(live[3])}
281	        old_values = {
282	            "type": row.type,
283	            "description": row.description,
284	            "owner": row.owner,
285	            "tags": json.loads(row.tags),
286	        }
287	        live_writes = {
288	            field: (seq, actor)
289	            for field, seq, actor in await store.fetchall(
290	                "SELECT field, seq, actor FROM field_writes WHERE node_id = ?", (holder,)
291	            )
292	        }
293	        old_writes = {field: (seq, actor) for field, (seq, actor) in json.loads(row.writes).items()}
294	
295	        filled: list[str] = []
296	        kept_live: list[str] = []
297	        not_restored: dict[str, Any] = {}
298	        take_value: list[str] = []
299	        take_write: list[str] = []
300	        for field in WRITTEN_FIELDS:
301	            old_w, live_w = old_writes.get(field), live_writes.get(field)
302	            old_is_newer = old_w is not None and (live_w is None or old_w[0] > live_w[0])
303	            differs = old_values[field] != live_values[field]
304	            if field == "type" and not differs:
305	                # Same type either way: nothing to report. Keep the newest report time for later merges.
306	                if old_is_newer:
307	                    take_write.append(field)
308	                continue
309	            if old_is_newer:
310	                filled.append(field)
311	                take_value.append(field)
312	                take_write.append(field)
313	            else:
314	                kept_live.append(field)
315	                if old_w is not None and differs:
316	                    not_restored[field] = old_values[field]
317	
318	        prior = {
319	            field: {"value": live_values[field], "write": list(live_writes[field]) if field in live_writes else None}
320	            for field in take_write
321	        }
322	        # A filled field that overwrote a value someone had written on the live node: show what was there.
323	        replaced = {
324	            field: live_values[field]
325	            for field in take_value
326	            if field in live_writes and live_values[field] != old_values[field]
327	        }
328	        if take_value:
329	            assignments = ", ".join(f"{field} = ?" for field in take_value)
330	            params = [tags_json(old_values[f]) if f == "tags" else old_values[f] for f in take_value]
331	            await store.write(f"UPDATE nodes SET {assignments} WHERE id = ?", (*params, holder))
332	        for field in take_write:
333	            seq, actor = old_writes[field]
334	            await record_write(store, holder, field, seq, actor)
335	        detail: dict[str, Any] = {"filled": filled, "kept_live": kept_live, "not_restored": not_restored}
336	        if replaced:
337	            detail["replaced"] = replaced
338	        return detail, prior
339	
340	    # ---- journal rows ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
341	
342	    async def _node_row(self, delete_op: str, node_id: str) -> NodeRow | None:
343	        row = await self.store.fetchone(NODE_ROW_SQL, (delete_op, node_id))
344	        return None if row is None else NodeRow(*row)
345	
346	    async def _edge_pending(self, delete_op: str, edge: Edge, retrying_for: str | None) -> bool:
347	        row = await self.store.fetchone(
348	            "SELECT outcome, waiting_on FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? AND from_id = ? AND to_id = ? "
349	            "AND type = ?",
350	            (delete_op, *edge),
351	        )
352	        return row is not None and _pending(row[0], row[1], retrying_for)
353	
354	    async def _mark_node(
355	        self,
356	        row: NodeRow,
357	        outcome: str,
358	        reason: str | None = None,
359	        *,
360	        merged_into: str | None = None,
361	        waiting_on: str | None = None,
362	        detail: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
363	        prior: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
364	    ) -> None:
365	        await self.store.write(
366	            "UPDATE removed_nodes SET outcome = ?, reason = ?, merged_into = ?, waiting_on = ?, detail = ?, "
367	            "decided_by = ?, prior = ? WHERE delete_op = ? AND id = ?",
368	            (
369	                outcome,
370	                reason,
371	                merged_into,
372	                waiting_on,
373	                None if detail is None else json.dumps(detail, ensure_ascii=False),
374	                self.undo_id,
375	                None if prior is None else json.dumps(prior, ensure_ascii=False),
376	                row.delete_op,
377	                row.id,
378	            ),
379	        )
380	
381	    async def _mark_edge(
382	        self,
383	        delete_op: str,
384	        edge: Edge,
385	        outcome: str,
386	        reason: str | None = None,
387	        *,
388	        now: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
389	        waiting_on: str | None = None,
390	    ) -> None:
391	        await self.store.write(
392	            "UPDATE removed_edges SET outcome = ?, reason = ?, waiting_on = ?, now_from = ?, now_to = ?, decided_by = ? "
393	            "WHERE delete_op = ? AND from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ?",
394	            (outcome, reason, waiting_on, *(now or (None, None)), self.undo_id, delete_op, *edge),
395	        )
396	
397	
398	# ---- report --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
399	
400	
401	async def build_report(store: Store, op_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
402	    """The report is a printout of the delete's journal rows: one entry per removed node and arrow."""
403	    node_rows = await store.fetchall(
404	        "SELECT id, qualified_name, outcome, reason, merged_into, waiting_on, detail "
405	        "FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? ORDER BY ord",
406	        (op_id,),
407	    )
408	    edge_rows = await store.fetchall(
409	        "SELECT from_id, to_id, type, outcome, reason, waiting_on, now_from, now_to "
410	        "FROM removed_edges WHERE delete_op = ? ORDER BY ord",
411	        (op_id,),
412	    )
413	    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
414	    for node_id, name, outcome, reason, merged_into, waiting_on, detail in node_rows:
415	        entry: dict[str, Any] = {"id": node_id, "qualified_name": name, "outcome": outcome}
416	        if reason is not None:
417	            entry["reason"] = reason
418	        if merged_into is not None:
419	            entry["merged_into"] = merged_into
420	        if detail is not None:
421	            entry.update(json.loads(detail))
422	        if waiting_on is not None:
423	            entry["waiting_on"] = waiting_on
424	        nodes.append(entry)
425	    edges: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
426	    for from_id, to_id, edge_type, outcome, reason, waiting_on, now_from, now_to in edge_rows:
427	        entry = {"from": from_id, "to": to_id, "type": edge_type, "outcome": outcome}
428	        if reason is not None:
429	            entry["reason"] = reason
430	        if now_from is not None and outcome != RESTORED:
431	            entry["now"] = [now_from, now_to]
432	        if waiting_on is not None:
433	            entry["waiting_on"] = waiting_on
434	        edges.append(entry)
435	    summary = {"nodes": _count(nodes), "edges": _count(edges)}
436	    return {"op_id": op_id, "summary": summary, "nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}
437	
438	
439	def _count(entries: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, int]:
440	    counts = {RESTORED: 0, MERGED: 0, SKIPPED: 0}
441	    for entry in entries:
442	        counts[entry["outcome"]] += 1
443	    return counts
444	
445	
446	def format_report(report: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
447	    """JSON with one node or arrow per line, so the report reads like a table and diffs cleanly."""
448	
449	    def block(key: str) -> str:
450	        items = report[key]
451	        if not items:
452	            return f'  "{key}": []'
453	        body = ",\n".join("    " + json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False) for item in items)
454	        return f'  "{key}": [\n{body}\n  ]'
455	
456	    head = [
457	        f'  "op_id": {json.dumps(report["op_id"])}',
458	        f'  "summary": {json.dumps(report["summary"])}',
459	    ]
460	    return "{\n" + ",\n".join(head + [block("nodes"), block("edges")]) + "\n}\n"

1	"""The tables of the database file: the live graph, and the journal undo reads and marks off."""
2	
3	SCHEMA = """
4	-- The live graph. dump prints these two tables and nothing else.
5	CREATE TABLE nodes (
6	    id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
7	    qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- the table holds live nodes only: a name is unique among live nodes
8	    type           TEXT NOT NULL,
9	    description    TEXT,
10	    owner          TEXT,
11	    tags           TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON list, set by people, in the order written
12	    effective_tags TEXT NOT NULL           -- JSON list, worked out, sorted
13	);
14	
15	CREATE TABLE edges (
16	    from_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id),
17	    to_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id),
18	    type    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('contains', 'references')),
19	    PRIMARY KEY (from_id, to_id, type)
20	);
21	-- A node has at most one contains parent: the contains arrows form a tree.
22	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_parent ON edges(to_id) WHERE type = 'contains';
23	CREATE INDEX edges_by_to ON edges(to_id, type);
24	
25	-- Every operation, applied or rejected. seq is the running number: "after the delete" means a larger seq.
26	-- Each undo is logged here too, once, as op_id 'undo:<op_id of the delete>' with kind 'undo', by a person,
27	-- so a later operation (or a redo) can tell what came after it.
28	CREATE TABLE ops (
29	    seq        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
30	    op_id      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
31	    kind       TEXT NOT NULL,
32	    actor      TEXT NOT NULL,
33	    applied_at TEXT NOT NULL,
34	    status     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('applied', 'rejected')),
35	    reason     TEXT,
36	    payload    TEXT NOT NULL
37	);
38	
39	-- Who wrote each field of each node last, and in which operation (seq 0 = the seed).
40	-- Tells "empty because nobody wrote it" from "a person cleared it on purpose".
41	-- Rows outlive their node, so a node restored with its old id keeps its write history.
42	CREATE TABLE field_writes (
43	    node_id TEXT NOT NULL,
44	    field   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (field IN ('description', 'owner', 'tags', 'type')),
45	    seq     INTEGER NOT NULL,
46	    actor   TEXT NOT NULL,
47	    PRIMARY KEY (node_id, field)
48	);
49	
50	-- Every arrow a person re-pointed away from its old end, with the operation's seq.
51	CREATE TABLE edge_removals (
52	    from_id TEXT NOT NULL,
53	    to_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
54	    type    TEXT NOT NULL,
55	    seq     INTEGER NOT NULL,
56	    actor   TEXT NOT NULL,
57	    op_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
58	    PRIMARY KEY (from_id, to_id, type, seq)
59	);
60	
61	-- A copy of each node a delete removed, and what undo decided for it.
62	CREATE TABLE removed_nodes (
63	    delete_op      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES ops(op_id),
64	    ord            INTEGER NOT NULL,       -- parents first
65	    id             TEXT NOT NULL,
66	    qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL,
67	    type           TEXT NOT NULL,
68	    description    TEXT,
69	    owner          TEXT,
70	    tags           TEXT NOT NULL,
71	    parent_id      TEXT,                   -- the contains parent at the time of the delete
72	    writes         TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON {field: [seq, actor]}, copied from field_writes
73	    outcome        TEXT CHECK (outcome IN ('restored', 'merged', 'skipped')),
74	    reason         TEXT,
75	    merged_into    TEXT,
76	    waiting_on     TEXT,                   -- the delete that has to be undone before this row can come back
77	    detail         TEXT,                   -- JSON for merged rows: filled, kept_live, not_restored, replaced
78	    decided_by     TEXT,                   -- the undo that wrote the outcome ('undo:<op_id>'; a retry names a later one)
79	    prior          TEXT,                   -- JSON for merged rows: {field: {value, write}} the live node held before
80	                                           -- undo changed it, so a redo can put it back
81	    PRIMARY KEY (delete_op, id)
82	);
83	CREATE INDEX removed_nodes_by_id ON removed_nodes(id);
84	CREATE INDEX removed_nodes_waiting ON removed_nodes(waiting_on) WHERE outcome = 'skipped';
85	
86	-- A copy of each arrow a delete removed, and what undo decided for it.
87	CREATE TABLE removed_edges (
88	    delete_op  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES ops(op_id),
89	    ord        INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- arrows from parents in the order of their child, then the rest
90	    from_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
91	    to_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
92	    type       TEXT NOT NULL,
93	    outcome    TEXT CHECK (outcome IN ('restored', 'merged', 'skipped')),
94	    reason     TEXT,
95	    waiting_on TEXT,
96	    now_from   TEXT,                       -- where the arrow points now, once its ends were worked out
97	    now_to     TEXT,
98	    decided_by TEXT,                       -- the undo that wrote the outcome
99	    PRIMARY KEY (delete_op, from_id, to_id, type)
100	);
101	CREATE INDEX removed_edges_waiting ON removed_edges(waiting_on) WHERE outcome = 'skipped';
102	"""

1	"""apply: run ops.jsonl in order, one transaction per operation.
2	
3	Five kinds of operation, each carrying an actor (human or ingest):
4	
5	    edit_node       human           set description, owner and/or tags of one live node
6	    add_edge        human, ingest   add a contains or references arrow between two live nodes
7	    repoint_edge    human, ingest   move one end of a live arrow (new_from_id or new_to_id); counts as one
8	                                    arrow taken away (kept in edge_removals) and one added
9	    ingest_node     ingest          by qualified_name: update the type of the live node that has the name,
10	                                    or create a node with an id built from op_id and name, under its parent
11	                                    when that parent is live; never sets description, owner or tags
12	    delete_subtree  human, ingest   remove a node, everything it contains and every arrow touching them;
13	                                    all of it moves into the journal under the delete's op_id
14	
15	Who did an operation matters in two places only. Ingest never sets description, owner or tags, so an
16	edit_node from ingest is refused. People do not create nodes or set types, so an ingest_node from a person
17	is refused.
18	
19	An operation that cannot be applied as written (it names a node or arrow that is not live, it would give a
20	node a second parent or make a node its own ancestor, a field has the wrong shape, ...) is stored as
21	rejected, with the reason, and changes nothing. A loop never gets into the graph.
22	
23	An op_id names one operation. One already in the database is skipped when the line is that same operation,
24	so running apply again on the same file is harmless. If it was used for a different operation, apply stops
25	with an error before it changes anything.
26	"""

13	# A node and everything below it along contains arrows, each with its contains parent. UNION (not
14	# UNION ALL) drops a node it has already found, so the walk ends even if a contains loop ever existed.
15	SUBTREE_SQL = """
16	WITH RECURSIVE sub(id) AS (
17	    SELECT ?
18	    UNION
19	    SELECT e.to_id FROM edges e JOIN sub ON e.from_id = sub.id WHERE e.type = 'contains'
20	)
21	SELECT n.id, n.qualified_name, n.type, n.description, n.owner, n.tags, n.effective_tags,
22	       (SELECT p.from_id FROM edges p WHERE p.to_id = n.id AND p.type = 'contains')
23	FROM sub JOIN nodes n ON n.id = sub.id
24	"""
25	
26	# Walk up from the second id along contains arrows; 1 when the first id is on the way (or is the second).
27	ANCESTOR_OR_SELF_SQL = """
28	WITH RECURSIVE up(id) AS (
29	    SELECT ?2
30	    UNION
31	    SELECT e.from_id FROM edges e JOIN up ON e.to_id = up.id WHERE e.type = 'contains'
32	)
33	SELECT 1 FROM up WHERE id = ?1 LIMIT 1
34	"""

38	    id: str
39	    qualified_name: str
40	    type: str
41	    description: str | None
42	    owner: str | None
43	    tags: str
44	    effective_tags: str
45	    parent_id: str | None

48	def walk_down(roots: Iterable[str], children: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str | None]]:
49	    """Every node below the roots once, parents before children, as (node, parent). Siblings in id order."""
50	    queue: deque[tuple[str, str | None]] = deque((root, None) for root in roots)
51	    seen: set[str] = set()
52	    while queue:
53	        node, parent = queue.popleft()
54	        if node in seen:
55	            continue
56	        seen.add(node)
57	        yield node, parent
58	        queue.extend((child, node) for child in sorted(children.get(node, ())))

62	    """The rows of root and everything below it, and the children of each of them."""
63	    rows = [SubtreeRow(*row) for row in await store.fetchall(SUBTREE_SQL, (root,))]

65	    for row in rows:

input.recap: The redo design matches the task's intent in its core rules, but I found four gaps that would give wrong results and a few smaller inconsistencies. Nothing was changed or run: redo is not built, so this is from reading the PDF, the design and the undo code.
input.ask: Should I write the fixes for points 1–4 into the design page?

message.content: The user hasn't heard from you in a while — say in a few words what you're doing, then continue.

content.text:
All four use the six-node example: `sales` contains `sales.orders` and `sales.refunds`, `sales.orders` contains `email` and `total`, and `reports.daily` references `sales.orders` and `total`.

## 1. Redo leaves skipped rows waiting

**Situation** (your story "The parent is deleted later"):

1. d1 deletes `sales.orders` with `email` and `total`.
2. d2 deletes `sales`, which takes `sales.refunds` with it.
3. `undo d1`: the parent `sales` is not live, so every row of d1 is skipped with `waiting_on: d2`. The graph does not change.
4. `redo d1`: the person decides d1 should stand after all.
5. `undo d2`: `sales` and `sales.refunds` come back.

**Issue:** in step 4, redo finds no restored nodes, no merges and no added arrows, so by the design every row is "unchanged, nothing to take back". The rows stay skipped and still wait on d2. In step 5, undo d2 retries every row that waits on d2 ([undo.py:124](graph_undo/undo.py:124)) and restores `sales.orders`, `email`, `total` and their arrows. The person's last word on d1 was redo, yet d1's content is back.

A skipped row that waits is a promise to come back when the other delete is undone. Redo has to cancel that promise, and the design only resets rows for removed nodes.

**Same cause, second symptom** (your usual story):

1. `undo d1` merges old `email` (n3) into n8 with nothing filled.
2. `redo d1` reports n3 as "unchanged, nothing_filled", and the row still says "merged into n8".
3. Someone deletes n8.
4. `undo d1` again: only rows with no outcome are decided, so n3 is passed over.

The name `sales.orders.email` is free and its parent is live, so invariant 2 says n3 must be restored, and it is not. The report also lists a merge into a node that is not live, which your check 4 rejects.

**Fix:** one rule. After redo, every row the undo decided is either kept (still live, outcome stays) or open again, with no outcome and no `waiting_on`.

## 2. Rounds are not defined

A round is one undo plus its redo. The design names the second round `undo:d1:2` and `redo:d1:2`, but leaves three things open.

- **Repeat or new round.** `undo d1` run twice in a row must write nothing (invariant 6). `undo d1` after a redo must be a real undo. The design never says how the tool tells them apart, and the code always uses `undo:d1` ([undo.py:118](graph_undo/undo.py:118)). The rule needed: look at the newest undo or redo entry in `ops` for this delete. If it is the same command, this call repeats or resumes it. If it is the other command, a new round starts.

- **Old redo outcomes block the next redo.**
  1. Round 1: undo restores `total`, redo removes it. The row gets redo outcome "removed".
  2. Round 2: undo restores `total` again.
  3. `redo d1`: the design says a run skips every row that already has a redo outcome. `total` has one from round 1, so it is skipped and stays live.

  So "undo and redo can go back and forth" fails on the second redo. Either undo clears the redo outcome when it decides a row again, or each redo outcome carries its round and only this round's are skipped.

- **A crash, then the other command.** `CRASH_AFTER=5 undo d1` stops with half the nodes back, and the person runs `redo d1` instead of finishing. The design says only an undone delete can be redone, and does not say whether a half-undone one counts. The mirror case is a crashed redo followed by `undo d1`: a repeat would write nothing and leave the graph half redone. The simplest rule is that each command refuses while the other is unfinished. That needs a "finished" mark on the entry in `ops`, because today the entry is written when the undo starts.

A smaller point: an op_id can be any string, so `undo:d1:2` could also mean round 1 of a delete named `d1:2`. Keeping the delete and the round number as separate values avoids parsing the name.

## 3. Which rows a redo owns

**Situation** (the parent story again, both deletes undone):

1. d1 deletes `sales.orders`, d2 deletes `sales`.
2. `undo d1`: everything waits on d2.
3. `undo d2`: restores `sales`, then retries d1's rows and restores them. Each of those rows now records `decided_by: undo:d2`.
4. The person wants `sales.orders` gone again but `sales` kept, and runs `redo d1`.

**Issue:** redo takes "every row that the undo of this delete decided". No row is still marked as decided by undo d1, so `redo d1` does nothing. The only command that removes `sales.orders` is `redo d2`, which also removes `sales` and `sales.refunds`. The state "d2 undone, d1 redone" cannot be reached.

Had the undos run in the other order, d2 then d1, the same graph would result but d1's rows would belong to undo d1, and `redo d1` would work. The outcome depends on a past order the person cannot see.

The text also reads two ways. Step 1 says redo takes "the delete's own rows". The story "Or: redo d1" says an arrow that is d1's own row is not taken back, because undo d2 put it there.

**Two ways to settle it:**

- **By delete (my recommendation).** `redo d1` covers every row of d1 that is currently put back, whoever decided it, plus rows of other deletes that undo d1 retried. In the parent story it removes `sales.orders` and leaves `sales`. In "Or: redo d1" the two arrows from `reports.daily` go out with their nodes and nothing is kept, so that step of the story changes.
- **By decider (what the story shows).** Keep it, add the parent case as a story, and have `redo d1` say why it did nothing.

I prefer the first because the undo report already works that way: a retried row keeps its entry in the report of its own delete.

## 4. Later changes in the way: my opinions

- **A restored node was deleted again by a newer delete d3.** Redo should leave it alone: outcome `unchanged`, reason `deleted_since`, naming d3. The d1 row should be opened like any other. A later `undo d1` then restores the node from d1's copy, which invariant 2 requires since the name is free. A later `undo d3` merges its newer copy in by "most recent write wins". This merges a node into its own id, which the code looks able to handle, but it needs one test.

- **The merge target is no longer live.** Say n7 was deleted by d3 after undo filled its description. Redo should report `unchanged`, reason `target_not_live`, and open the row. I would not reach into d3's journal to take the filled value out, because a journal should stay a true copy of what its delete removed. The cost is that undoing d3 later brings n7 back with that description. That is acceptable as long as the report shows it.

- **One undo restored a node and another undo merged into it.** For example, undo d2 restores n7, undo d1 merges old n2 into it, then `redo d2` runs. n7 passes both tests, because the filled field carries its old write number and nothing is attached. It would be removed, carrying d1's restored description with it. I would keep it, reason `still_in_use`, whenever a standing merge from another undo points at it. This fits your "redo the newest undo first" rule: `redo d1` reverts the fill, then `redo d2` removes n7 cleanly.

Each of these needs a defined outcome, so the report covers every row once and redo never trips on a missing node. Given the time limit, I would add one small-fixture test for the first case, since deleting again is the likeliest, and one sentence each for the other two.

Which of these do you want written into the design page?

553

4How redo works

554

Redo is the one extension the task names. This section is its design. The tool's four commands do not include it yet, but undo already records everything redo needs.

555

redo <op_id> takes the op_id of a subtree delete that has been undone, and applies the delete again to the graph as it is now. It does not replay the delete from scratch. It takes back what the undo put back: restored nodes go out again, the arrows undo added are removed, and the fields undo filled get the value they had before. Like undo, it never removes or changes anything a person did in the meantime. For redo, "in the meantime" means after the undo.

556

Pick a story, then step through it. Each one starts where an undo left the graph.

557 558
559
Story
560
Step
561

562 574
575
576
577 578

What redo does, in order

579
    580
  1. Take every row that the undo of this delete decided. That is the delete's own rows, plus any rows of earlier deletes that this undo retried.
    2. 581
  2. Take the nodes undo restored, children before parents. For each one decide removed or kept (next figure). A removed node goes back into the journal together with every arrow that touches it. That is one transaction.
    3. 582
  3. For each node undo merged, put back the fields undo filled, then refresh the tags of the live node and everything below it.
    4. 583
  4. Take the remaining arrows undo added, the ones between nodes that stay, and remove them.
    5. 584
  5. Record the redo as an operation of its own and print the report.
    6. 585
586

The order is undo's order turned around. Undo goes parents first, because a child needs its parent to attach to. Redo goes children first, because a parent can only leave once nothing is left under it.

587 588 613 614

Taking a restored node out again

615

A node undo restored is removed again when both of these hold. Otherwise it is kept, and the report gives the reason.

616
    617
  • No person has written it since it came back. field_writes holds the number of the last write to each field, and the undo has a number of its own in ops. A write by a person with a larger number came after the undo. Reason when it fails: written_since_undo.
    • 618
  • Nothing else is attached to it. Every child and every arrow that touches it must be one this redo is taking out as well. A node created or moved under it since, an arrow a person or the ingest added to it since, a child that was itself kept, or something another undo put there, all keep it in place. Reason: still_in_use.
    • 619
620

A removed node goes back into the journal of its delete, and its name is free again. The journal copy is refreshed from the live node as it leaves. If the ingest reported a new type for the node while it was back, that type is not lost. A write by the ingest does not keep a node in place: it only happened because the node was there, and the next ingest run recreates the node if the source still has it.

621

What a row goes back to depends on whose row it is:

622
    623
  • A row of this delete has no outcome again, as it was right after the delete. So undo can run again later and decides the row afresh against the graph of that moment.
    • 624
  • A row of an earlier delete that this undo retried goes back to skipped, waiting_on this delete. That is what it was before the undo.
    • 625
626 627

Putting filled fields back

628

When undo merged an old node into a live one, it filled some fields of the live node and saved what they held before in prior: the value, and who wrote it and when. Redo goes through the filled fields one at a time:

629
    630
  • The field is still as undo left it. Redo puts back the earlier value and the earlier write record. Most of the time the earlier value is "empty, nobody wrote it". Example: the description and the tag pii on the new sales.orders.
    • 631
  • A person has written the field since the undo. It stays as the person wrote it. Reason: written_since_undo.
    • 632
633

Undo copied the old write record along with the value, so "still as undo left it" is a plain comparison: the field's write record is still the one undo copied. Fields undo did not fill were never touched and are not touched now. Inherited tags are recomputed, as always: when pii leaves the live node, it leaves everything below it.

634 635

Arrows

636
    637
  • removed: undo added the arrow, and it goes out again. This covers an arrow that touches a removed node, and an arrow undo re-aimed at a node that stays. Example: reports.daily → n7.
    • 638
  • kept, reason end_kept: the arrow touches a restored node that redo kept. A node that stays keeps the arrows undo gave it, so it is not left half connected.
    • 639
  • unchanged, reason not_added_by_undo: undo found the arrow already there, or skipped it. There is nothing to take back.
    • 640
  • unchanged, reason changed_since_undo: someone re-pointed the arrow away after the undo. Whether it is there now or not is their doing, so redo leaves it as it is.
    • 641
642 643

Work done between the undo and the redo

644

The same three kinds as for undo, each with one rule.

645
    646
  • Independent. It touched something undo did not put back. Rule: left exactly as it is.
    • 647
  • Conflicting. A person wrote on, or attached something to, a thing undo put back. Example: a person rewrote the description of the restored sales.orders.total. Rule: that thing stays, with everything it needs to stay whole: its parents and its arrows. The report lists it as kept.
    • 648
  • Caused. It happened only because the undo happened. Example: the ingest found sales.orders.total live again and updated its type instead of creating a new node. Rule: it does not hold redo back, and the journal copy keeps the newer type.
    • 649
650

Redo only takes back rows undo decided, and only while they are as undo left them. It never overwrites or removes anything a person did after the undo.

651 652

Redo, undo, and their order

653
    654
  • Redo straight after undo gives back the graph from before the undo. Nothing has changed in between, so every row is taken back. The dump is the same, byte for byte, as the dump taken just before the undo.
    • 655
  • Undo can run again after a redo. The rows redo took back have no outcome, so undo decides them like new rows. With nothing changed in between, it gives the same graph as the first undo.
    • 656
  • Only an undone delete can be redone. For a delete that was never undone, for any other operation, or for an id that does not exist, redo prints an error and writes nothing.
    • 657
  • After several undos, redo the newest undo first. If an older undo is redone while a newer one still stands, some of its nodes may carry arrows or children the newer undo put there. Those nodes are kept, reason still_in_use. Redone newest first, nothing is kept for this reason. This mirrors undo, where the newest delete undone first means nothing waits.
    • 658
  • Each round has its own entry in ops. The first undo of d1 is undo:d1 and its redo is redo:d1. A second round is undo:d1:2 and redo:d1:2. Every row names the undo that decided it, so "since it came back" always has an exact meaning.
    • 659
660 661

Crashes and running it twice

662
    663
  • One row, one transaction, as for undo. The graph change, the tag refresh and the row's redo outcome are saved together or not at all.
    • 664
  • Each journal row gets a redo outcome next to its undo outcome: removed, kept or unchanged for nodes and arrows, and reverted for a merged node, with a reason. The report is a printout of those.
    • 665
  • Crash and resume. CRASH_AFTER=<n> works for redo as it does for undo. A resumed run skips every row that already has a redo outcome.
    • 666
  • Run it twice. The second run finds a redo outcome on every row, writes nothing, and prints the same report.
    • 667
668 669

The report for the first story

670

687 688

What the checker would test

689
    690
  1. No change made by a person after the undo is lost or altered by the redo. Tested like check 1, with a dump just before the redo and one just after.
    2. 691
  2. Redo straight after undo gives the dump from before the undo, byte for byte. A second undo then gives the dump from after the first undo.
    3. 692
  3. The report accounts for every row the undo decided, exactly once, and each outcome agrees with the dump: a removed row is gone, a kept row is there, a reverted field holds its earlier value.
    4. 693
  4. The graph stays whole. No two live nodes share a name, no arrow points at a missing node, and inherited tags are correct.
    5. 694
  5. Redo is idempotent and resumable, tested as checks 6 and 7 are for undo.
    6. 695
696

Each redo story above becomes a test in the small fixture, the same way the undo stories did.

content.text:
All examples use the same small graph: `sales` contains `sales.orders` and `sales.refunds`; `sales.orders` contains `email` and `total`; `reports.daily` has reference arrows to `sales.orders` and `total`.

## 2. Solutions for each rounds problem

**Problem A: the tool cannot tell a repeat from a new round.**
When `undo d1` is typed, look in `ops` for the newest undo or redo entry about d1:
- No entry: this is the first undo. Record it as round 1.
- The newest entry is an undo: this is a repeat or a resume. Record nothing and only decide rows that have no outcome.
- The newest entry is a redo: this is a new round. Record a new undo entry with the next round number.

`redo d1` uses the same rule mirrored. No undo entry means an error. Newest is an undo means a new redo. Newest is a redo means a repeat or resume.

**Problem B: an old redo outcome makes the next redo skip the row.**
Store next to each redo outcome which redo wrote it, the same way `decided_by` already names the undo. A redo then skips only rows that carry its own name. A row marked by an earlier redo is decided again. This also lets a later redo reconsider a node that an earlier redo kept.

**Problem C: a crash, then the other command.**
Give each undo and redo entry a "finished" mark, written in its last transaction. Before starting, each command checks the newest entry of the other kind. If that one is unfinished, the command refuses, writes nothing, and says "undo d1 is not finished, run it again first". The person finishes it by running the same command again, which already works.

**Problem D: the name `undo:d1:2` can clash with a delete named `d1:2`.**
Do not read meaning out of the name. Store the delete's op_id and the round number as separate values on the entry, and let rows point at the entry's running number in `ops`.

## 3. Full context

**The question:** when someone types `redo d1`, which things should redo take out of the graph again? With one delete the answer is easy: whatever undo d1 put back. With two deletes it gets harder, because of a rule in your undo design.

**The rule that causes it:** sometimes undo d1 cannot put a node back because its parent is missing. Your design marks it "skipped, waiting on d2". When d2 is undone later, undo d2 puts that node back on d1's behalf.

**The story, step by step:**
1. d1 deletes `sales.orders` with `email` and `total`.
2. d2 deletes `sales` with `sales.refunds`. Only `reports.daily` is left.
3. `undo d1`: the parent `sales` is gone, so nothing can come back. All of d1's nodes wait on d2.
4. `undo d2`: `sales` and `sales.refunds` come back. Then undo d2 brings back the waiting nodes `sales.orders`, `email` and `total`. The whole graph is back.
5. The person decides `sales.orders` should be deleted after all, and types `redo d1`.

**What the design does at step 5:** redo d1 looks for things that the command "undo d1" put back. That command put nothing back; undo d2 did all of it. So redo d1 finds nothing and does nothing.

**Why that is a problem:**
- The person cannot get what they want. The only command that removes `sales.orders` is `redo d2`, and it removes `sales` and `sales.refunds` too.
- If the two undos had been typed in the other order, undo d1 would have done the restoring itself and `redo d1` would work. The graph is the same but the command gives a different result.

**My solution:** `redo d1` should take out everything that delete d1 removed and that is back now, whichever undo command brought it back.

**What that gives:**
- In the story above, `redo d1` removes `sales.orders`, `email` and `total`. `sales` and `sales.refunds` stay.
- `redo d2` still removes `sales` and `sales.refunds`. If nodes of d1 are still back at that moment, they return to "waiting on d2", as your design already says.

**What would change in the design:** the first step of "What redo does, in order", the step "Or: redo d1" in the last story, and one new story for the case above.

## 4. The three cases in detail

In each case, something changed between the undo and the redo, so redo does not find what undo left.

**Case A: the node undo restored has been deleted again.**
1. d1 deletes `sales.orders`, `email` and `total`.
2. `undo d1` restores all three.
3. Someone deletes `total` on its own. Call this delete d3. `total` is now in d3's journal.
4. `redo d1` wants to take out the three nodes undo restored, but `total` is not in the graph.

The design has no instruction for this. My suggestion: redo removes `sales.orders` and `email` as normal and reports `total` as unchanged, reason `deleted_since`, naming d3. One thing to decide when building: if d1 is undone again later, `total` comes back even though d3 deleted it. Invariant 2 asks for that, but the checker's "nodes a person deleted stay deleted" test would need to allow it.

**Case B: the node whose fields undo filled has been deleted.**
A reminder of what a merge is: after d1, the ingest recreates `sales.orders` as a new node n7 with an empty description. Undo d1 cannot bring the old node back because the name is taken, so it copies the old description into n7. Redo should empty that description again.
1. d1 deletes `sales.orders`.
2. The ingest recreates it as n7.
3. `undo d1` fills n7's description with "One row per order".
4. Someone deletes n7. Call this d3. n7 goes into d3's journal with the filled description.
5. `redo d1` wants to empty n7's description, but n7 is not in the graph.

There are two choices: do nothing, or reach into d3's journal and empty the description there. I suggest doing nothing and reporting unchanged, reason `target_not_live`. A journal should stay an exact copy of what its delete removed. The cost is that if d3 is undone later, n7 returns with the description still filled.

**Case C: two undos worked on the same node.**
1. d1 deletes `sales.orders.email`, description "Customer email".
2. The ingest recreates it as n8, with an empty description.
3. Someone deletes n8. Call this d2.
4. `undo d2` restores n8, still empty.
5. `undo d1` finds the name taken by n8, so it fills n8's description with "Customer email".
6. `redo d2` asks whether n8 should go out again.

At step 6 the design has two tests. Has a person written on n8 since it came back? No, because a filled value counts as its old, original write. Is anything attached to it? No. So n8 is removed. But undo d1 is still in force, and the description it restored disappears with n8. My suggestion: add a third reason to keep a node. If another undo that still stands has merged into it, it is kept, reason `still_in_use`. The clean order is `redo d1` first, which empties the description, then `redo d2`, which removes n8.

Which of 2, 3 and 4 should I write into the design?

One kind of row is not opened. A row of another delete that an undo of this delete retried goes back to skipped, waiting_on this delete. That is what it was before the undo, and its own delete is still undone. The report lists these rows apart from the delete's own rows, each with the delete it belongs to.

When a later delete got there first

Between the undo and the redo, a person can delete something undo put back. It is then in the journal of that later delete, here d3. Redo never takes back a person's delete, and never edits the journal of another delete.

  • A node undo restored is already gone. Example: undo d1 restored sales.orders.total, then d3 deleted it on its own. Redo d1 has nothing to remove. Outcome unchanged, reason deleted_since, and the report names d3. The row is opened like the others. Its journal copy is refreshed from the copy d3 holds, so the journal of d1 has the node as it last was.
  • The node undo filled is already gone. Example: undo d1 filled the description of n7, then d3 deleted n7. Redo cannot put the field back, because n7 is not in the graph. Outcome unchanged, reason target_not_live, naming d3. The copy of n7 in the journal of d3 keeps the filled value. An undo of d3 has to bring n7 back with the fields it had when d3 removed it, so that copy is left as it is.
  • An arrow undo added is already gone, because d3 removed one of its ends. Outcome unchanged, reason deleted_since.

Such a node is now covered by two deletes, and undoing either one brings it back. A new undo of d1 finds the name free and the parent live, so it restores the node. That is the rule of undo, and it holds here too: the redo applied d1 again, and d1 covers this node. An undo of d3 after that finds the node live under the same id and has nothing to add. The small fixture gets one test for the first case.

Those nodes are kept, reason still_in_use. Redone newest first, nothing is kept for this reason. This mirrors undo, where the newest delete undone first means nothing waits.

    • Going back and forth

    A person can undo, redo, undo again and redo again. One undo and the redo that follows it is a round.

    • Each undo and each redo has its own entry in ops. The entry stores which delete it is for and which round it is, as values of their own. Its name (undo:d1, redo:d1) is only a label, and nothing is read out of it, so a delete with an unusual op_id cannot be mixed up with a round. A journal row points at the entry that decided it by the entry's running number, so "since it came back" always has an exact meaning.
    • Repeat or new round. The same command can mean two things, so the tool looks at the newest undo or redo entry for the delete. For undo d1: with no entry, this is the first undo. If the newest entry is an undo, this call repeats or resumes it, so a finished undo writes nothing. If the newest entry is a redo, a new round starts. For redo d1: with no undo entry, it is an error. If the newest entry is an undo, this is the redo of that round. If the newest entry is a redo, this call repeats or resumes it.

The tool says which command to run again first, and writes nothing. A crashed run is always finished by running the same command again.
    • A redo outcome names the redo that wrote it. A redo skips only the rows that carry its own mark, and decides a row marked in an earlier round again. So a node that came back in a new round can go out again, and a node an earlier redo kept is looked at again.

"""The command line: load, apply, undo, dump.

    python3 graphundo.py [--db graph.db] load seed.jsonl
    python3 graphundo.py [--db graph.db] apply ops.jsonl
    python3 graphundo.py [--db graph.db] undo <op_id>      (reads CRASH_AFTER=<n>)
    python3 graphundo.py [--db graph.db] dump

The database path defaults to $GRAPHUNDO_DB, then graph.db in the current directory.
Exit codes: 0 done, 1 error (nothing written), 3 stopped by CRASH_AFTER.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
from typing import TextIO

from .applier import Applier
from .common import InputError
from .dumper import dump
from .loader import load
from .store import Store
from .undo import UndoError, format_report, undo


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="graphundo", description="Undo for subtree deletes in a shared graph.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        default=os.environ.get("GRAPHUNDO_DB", "graph.db"),
        help="SQLite file (default: $GRAPHUNDO_DB or graph.db)",
    )
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    commands.add_parser("load", help="create the database from a seed file").add_argument("seed")
    commands.add_parser("apply", help="apply operations in order").add_argument("ops")
    commands.add_parser("undo", help="undo one subtree delete and print the report").add_argument("op_id")
    commands.add_parser("dump", help="print the live graph as sorted JSONL")
    return parser


def _crash_after() -> int | None:
    raw = os.environ.get("CRASH_AFTER", "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return None
    try:
        value = int(raw)
    except ValueError:
        raise InputError(f"CRASH_AFTER must be a whole number, got {raw!r}") from None
    if value < 0:
        raise InputError(f"CRASH_AFTER must not be negative, got {value}")
    return value


def _write(stream: TextIO, text: str) -> None:
    stream.write(text)
    stream.flush()


async def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if args.command == "load":
        counts = await load(args.db, args.seed)
        await asyncio.to_thread(_write, sys.stdout, json.dumps(counts) + "\n")
        return 0

    if not await asyncio.to_thread(os.path.isfile, args.db):
        raise InputError(f"no database at {args.db}; run load first")
    crash_after = _crash_after() if args.command == "undo" else None  # only undo reads CRASH_AFTER
    store = await Store.open(args.db, crash_after=crash_after)
    try:
        if args.command == "apply":
            output = json.dumps(await Applier(store).apply_file(args.ops), indent=2) + "\n"
        elif args.command == "undo":
            output = format_report(await undo(store, args.op_id))
            await asyncio.to_thread(_write, sys.stderr, f"graphundo: undo {args.op_id}: {store.writes} writes\n")
        else:
            output = await dump(store)
        await asyncio.to_thread(_write, sys.stdout, output)
    finally:
        await store.close()
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return asyncio.run(_run(args))
    except (InputError, UndoError) as exc:
        print(f"graphundo: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except BrokenPipeError:
        return 1
"""Async access to the one SQLite file.

sqlite3 is a blocking library. Every call to it runs on one worker thread that owns the connection, and
callers await the result, so the event loop never waits on the disk. One thread also gives one connection
and a strict order of statements, which the per-step transactions rely on.

The store counts every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE it runs. When CRASH_AFTER=<n> is set (only undo passes it
in), the process stops at once right after the n-th write, before the step it belongs to is committed.
SQLite discards that half-done step the next time the file is opened.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import os
import sqlite3
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Iterable, Sequence
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import Any, TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")
Params = Sequence[Any]

CRASH_EXIT_CODE = 3


def _connect(path: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    # isolation_level=None: sqlite3 never opens a transaction on its own; every BEGIN/COMMIT is ours.
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")  # an arrow can never point at a node that is not there
    # SQLite's default rollback journal: every committed step is in the one database file. A transaction
    # cut short by a crash leaves a journal next to it, and SQLite rolls the step back the next time the
    # file is opened.
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = FULL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
    return conn


def _fetchall(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sql: str, params: Params) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
    return conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()


def _fetchone(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sql: str, params: Params) -> tuple[Any, ...] | None:
    return conn.execute(sql, params).fetchone()


class Store:
    """One open database file."""

    def __init__(
        self, path: str, executor: ThreadPoolExecutor, conn: sqlite3.Connection, crash_after: int | None
    ) -> None:
        self.path = path
        self._executor = executor
        self._conn = conn
        self._crash_after = crash_after
        self.writes = 0

    @classmethod
    async def open(cls, path: str, *, crash_after: int | None = None) -> Store:
        executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix="sqlite")
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        try:
            conn = await loop.run_in_executor(executor, _connect, path)
        except BaseException:
            executor.shutdown(wait=False)
            raise
        return cls(path, executor, conn, crash_after)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        try:
            await self._call(self._conn.close)
        finally:
            self._executor.shutdown(wait=True)

    async def _call(self, fn: Callable[..., T], *args: Any) -> T:
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        return await loop.run_in_executor(self._executor, fn, *args)

    # ---- reads -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def fetchall(self, sql: str, params: Params = ()) -> list[tuple[Any, ...]]:
        return await self._call(_fetchall, self._conn, sql, params)

    async def fetchone(self, sql: str, params: Params = ()) -> tuple[Any, ...] | None:
        return await self._call(_fetchone, self._conn, sql, params)

    async def fetchval(self, sql: str, params: Params = ()) -> Any:
        row = await self.fetchone(sql, params)
        return None if row is None else row[0]

    # ---- writes (counted) --------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def write(self, sql: str, params: Params = ()) -> int:
        """Run one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE. Returns the number of rows it changed."""
        return await self._call(self._write, sql, params)

    async def write_many(self, sql: str, rows: Iterable[Params]) -> None:
        await self._call(self._write_many, sql, list(rows))

    # ---- statements that are not writes to the data -------------------------------------------------

    async def control(self, sql: str) -> None:
        """SAVEPOINT, RELEASE, ROLLBACK TO, temp-table DDL. Not counted."""
        await self._call(self._conn.execute, sql)

    async def script(self, sql: str) -> None:
        await self._call(self._conn.executescript, sql)

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def transaction(self) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        """One step: everything inside is saved together or not at all."""
        await self._call(self._conn.execute, "BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            yield
        except BaseException:
            await self._call(self._conn.execute, "ROLLBACK")
            raise
        try:
            await self._call(self._conn.execute, "COMMIT")
        except BaseException:
            if self._conn.in_transaction:
                await self._call(self._conn.execute, "ROLLBACK")
            raise

    # ---- worker-thread side ------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _write(self, sql: str, params: Params) -> int:
        if self._crash_after is not None and self.writes >= self._crash_after:
            self._crash()  # only reached with CRASH_AFTER=0
        cursor = self._conn.execute(sql, params)
        self.writes += 1
        if self._crash_after is not None and self.writes >= self._crash_after:
            self._crash()
        return cursor.rowcount

    def _write_many(self, sql: str, rows: list[Params]) -> None:
        if self._crash_after is None:
            self._conn.executemany(sql, rows)
            self.writes += len(rows)
            return
        for row in rows:  # count each row, so CRASH_AFTER can land inside a batch
            self._write(sql, row)

    def _crash(self) -> None:
        message = (
            f"graphundo: CRASH_AFTER={self._crash_after}: stopping after {self.writes} writes; "
            "the step in progress is not committed\n"
        )
        os.write(2, message.encode())
        os._exit(CRASH_EXIT_CODE)  # no cleanup, no commit, no rollback: like a killed process
"""Names and small helpers shared by the tool's modules."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import datetime
import json
from collections.abc import Iterable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

HUMAN = "human"
INGEST = "ingest"
ACTORS = (HUMAN, INGEST)

CONTAINS = "contains"
EDGE_TYPES = (CONTAINS, "references")

# The three fields people write. Ingest never sets them.
AUTHORED = ("description", "owner", "tags")
# type is written by ingest (and by the seed). On merge it follows the same "most recent write wins" rule.
WRITTEN_FIELDS = AUTHORED + ("type",)


class InputError(Exception):
    """A file, argument or environment value the tool cannot use. Nothing has been written."""


def valid_value(field: str, value: Any) -> bool:
    """description and owner are a string or null; tags is a list of strings, kept exactly as written."""
    if field == "tags":
        return isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in value)
    return value is None or isinstance(value, str)


def utc_now() -> str:
    """The time an operation is logged, as stored in ops.applied_at."""
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")


def tags_json(tags: Iterable[str]) -> str:
    """The one way a tag list is stored, so stored text can be compared directly."""
    return json.dumps(list(tags), ensure_ascii=False)


async def read_jsonl(path: str | Path) -> list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Read a JSONL file off the event loop. Returns (line number, object) pairs; blank lines are ignored."""
    try:
        text = await asyncio.to_thread(Path(path).read_text, encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise InputError(f"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror or exc}") from exc
    records: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = []
    for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            value = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: not valid JSON ({exc.msg})") from exc
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            raise InputError(f"{path}:{lineno}: expected a JSON object")
        records.append((lineno, value))
    return records
"""Tag propagator.

effective_tags of a node = its own tags + the effective tags of its contains parent. Only contains arrows
carry tags. Inherited tags are never copied into the journal: they are always worked out from what is live.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence

from .common import tags_json
from .graph import subtree, walk_down
from .store import Store

PARENT_TAGS_SQL = """
SELECT p.effective_tags FROM edges e JOIN nodes p ON p.id = e.from_id
WHERE e.to_id = ? AND e.type = 'contains'
"""

ROOTS_SQL = "SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT to_id FROM edges WHERE type = 'contains') ORDER BY id"


def propagate(
    roots: Iterable[str],
    children: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]],
    own: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]],
    inherited: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]],
) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Each node takes its own tags plus the worked-out tags of its parent; a root starts from inherited."""
    result: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for node, parent in walk_down(roots, children):
        above = result[parent] if parent is not None else inherited.get(node, ())
        result[node] = sorted(set(own[node]) | set(above))
    return result


async def refresh_subtree(store: Store, root_id: str) -> None:
    """Recompute effective_tags for root_id and everything below it. Writes only the rows that change."""
    rows, children = await subtree(store, root_id)
    if not rows:
        return
    parent_tags = await store.fetchval(PARENT_TAGS_SQL, (root_id,))
    fresh = propagate(
        [root_id],
        children,
        {row.id: json.loads(row.tags) for row in rows},
        {root_id: json.loads(parent_tags) if parent_tags else []},
    )
    for row in sorted(rows):
        text = tags_json(fresh[row.id])
        if text != row.effective_tags:
            await store.write("UPDATE nodes SET effective_tags = ? WHERE id = ?", (text, row.id))


async def refresh_all(store: Store) -> None:
    """Recompute effective_tags for every live node: the same walk, from every node without a parent."""
    for (root,) in await store.fetchall(ROOTS_SQL):
        await refresh_subtree(store, root)
"""dump: the live graph as sorted JSONL.

Node lines sorted by id, then arrow lines sorted by from_id, to_id and type. Keys always in the same order.
Two equal graphs always print the same bytes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from .store import Store


async def dump(store: Store) -> str:
    nodes = await store.fetchall(
        "SELECT id, qualified_name, type, description, owner, tags, effective_tags FROM nodes ORDER BY id"
    )
    edges = await store.fetchall("SELECT from_id, to_id, type FROM edges ORDER BY from_id, to_id, type")
    lines = [
        json.dumps(
            {
                "id": node_id,
                "qualified_name": name,
                "type": node_type,
                "description": description,
                "owner": owner,
                "tags": json.loads(tags),
                "effective_tags": json.loads(effective),
            },
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
        for node_id, name, node_type, description, owner, tags, effective in nodes
    ]
    lines.extend(
        json.dumps({"from_id": from_id, "to_id": to_id, "type": edge_type}, ensure_ascii=False)
        for from_id, to_id, edge_type in edges
    )
    return "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)

2	
3	checker.py replays the fixture here to know what each delete removed and who wrote what, and when.
4	gen_fixture.py applies every operation it writes here, so each one is valid when it runs and the planted
5	rejections really are rejected. Nothing here comes from the tool (graph_undo): the checker must share no
6	code with it, so the rules are written out a second time, independently.
7	"""

9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import uuid
12	from collections import defaultdict, deque
13	from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	# The repository's rule for the id of a node an ingest creates (README).
17	INGEST_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("2f0c9a52-8a4e-4c55-9d1b-1b0f6d1e7a3c")
18	AUTHORED = ("description", "owner", "tags")
19	EDGE_TYPES = ("contains", "references")
20	
21	Edge = tuple[str, str, str]
22	
23	
24	def ingest_node_id(op_id: str, qualified_name: str) -> str:
25	    return str(uuid.uuid5(INGEST_NAMESPACE, f"{op_id}/{qualified_name}"))
26	
27	
28	def walk_down(roots: Iterable[str], children: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> list[str]:
29	    """Every node below the roots once, parents before children, siblings in id order."""
30	    order: list[str] = []
31	    seen: set[str] = set()
32	    queue = deque(roots)
33	    while queue:
34	        node = queue.popleft()
35	        if node in seen:
36	            continue
37	        seen.add(node)
38	        order.append(node)
39	        queue.extend(sorted(children.get(node, ())))
40	    return order
41	
42	
43	class Replay:
44	    """The graph after the seed and each operation, plus who wrote what and when."""
45	
46	    def __init__(self, seed: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
47	        self.nodes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
48	        self.by_name: dict[str, str] = {}
49	        self.parent: dict[str, str] = {}
50	        self.refs: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
51	        self.writes: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[int, str]] = {}  # (node, field) -> (seq, actor); seed = 0
52	        self.edge_events: dict[Edge, list[tuple[int, str, str]]] = defaultdict(list)  # (seq, actor, add/remove)
53	        self.node_removals: dict[str, list[tuple[int, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
54	        self.deletes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}  # op_id -> seq, removed node snapshots, removed arrows
55	        self.status: dict[str, str] = {}  # op_id -> "applied" or "rejected:<reason>"
56	        records = list(seed)
57	        for rec in records:
58	            if rec["kind"] == "node":
59	                node_id = rec["id"]
60	                self.nodes[node_id] = {
61	                    "qualified_name": rec["qualified_name"],
62	                    "type": rec["type"],
63	                    "description": rec.get("description"),
64	                    "owner": rec.get("owner"),
65	                    "tags": list(rec.get("tags", [])),
66	                }
67	                self.by_name[rec["qualified_name"]] = node_id
68	                for field in AUTHORED + ("type",):
69	                    self.writes[(node_id, field)] = (0, "seed")
70	        for rec in records:
71	            if rec["kind"] == "edge":
72	                if rec["type"] == "contains":
73	                    self.parent[rec["to_id"]] = rec["from_id"]
74	                else:
75	                    self.refs.add((rec["from_id"], rec["to_id"]))
76	
77	    # ---- reading the graph ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	
79	    def edges(self) -> set[Edge]:
80	        return {(p, c, "contains") for c, p in self.parent.items()} | {(f, t, "references") for f, t in self.refs}
81	
82	    def has_edge(self, edge: Edge) -> bool:
83	        f, t, kind = edge
84	        return self.parent.get(t) == f if kind == "contains" else (f, t) in self.refs
85	
86	    def children(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
87	        out: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
88	        for child, parent in self.parent.items():
89	            out[parent].append(child)
90	        return out
91	
92	    def children_of(self, node: str) -> list[str]:
93	        return sorted(child for child, parent in self.parent.items() if parent == node)
94	
95	    def subtree(self, root: str) -> list[str]:
96	        return walk_down([root], self.children())
97	
98	    def ancestor_or_self(self, ancestor: str, node: str | None) -> bool:
99	        seen: set[str] = set()
100	        while node is not None and node not in seen:
101	            if node == ancestor:
102	                return True
103	            seen.add(node)
104	            node = self.parent.get(node)
105	        return False
106	
107	    # ---- operations ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
108	
109	    def apply_all(self, ops: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
110	        for seq, op in enumerate(ops, start=1):
111	            self.apply(seq, op)
112	
113	    def apply(self, seq: int, op: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
114	        """Apply one operation. Returns None, or the reason it is rejected (then nothing changes)."""
115	        actor, kind = op.get("actor"), op.get("kind")
116	        handler = {
117	            "edit_node": self._edit,
118	            "add_edge": self._add_edge,
119	            "repoint_edge": self._repoint,
120	            "ingest_node": self._ingest,
121	            "delete_subtree": self._delete,
122	        }.get(kind)
123	        if actor not in ("human", "ingest"):
124	            reason = "unknown_actor"
125	        elif handler is None:
126	            reason = "unknown_kind"
127	        else:
128	            reason = handler(seq, op, actor)
129	        self.status[op["op_id"]] = "applied" if reason is None else f"rejected:{reason}"
130	        return reason
131	
132	    def _add(self, edge: Edge, seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
133	        f, t, kind = edge
134	        if kind == "contains":
135	            self.parent[t] = f
136	        else:
137	            self.refs.add((f, t))
138	        self.edge_events[edge].append((seq, actor, "add"))
139	
140	    def _remove(self, edge: Edge, seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
141	        f, t, kind = edge
142	        if kind == "contains":
143	            del self.parent[t]
144	        else:
145	            self.refs.discard((f, t))
146	        self.edge_events[edge].append((seq, actor, "remove"))
147	
148	    def _new_arrow_problem(self, edge: Edge, *, child_moves: bool = False) -> str | None:
149	        f, t, kind = edge
150	        if self.has_edge(edge):
151	            return "edge_exists"
152	        if kind == "contains":
153	            if not child_moves and t in self.parent:
154	                return "child_has_parent"
155	            if self.ancestor_or_self(t, f):
156	                return "would_create_cycle"
157	        return None
158	
159	    @staticmethod
160	    def _text(op: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> str | None:
161	        value = op.get(key)
162	        return value if isinstance(value, str) and value else None
163	
164	    def _edit(self, seq: int, op: dict[str, Any], actor: str) -> str | None:
165	        if actor != "human":
166	            return "actor_not_allowed"
167	        node, changes = self._text(op, "id"), op.get("set")
168	        if node is None or not isinstance(changes, dict) or not changes:
169	            return "malformed"
170	        for field, value in changes.items():
171	            if field not in AUTHORED:
172	                return "malformed"
173	            if field == "tags":
174	                if not isinstance(value, list) or not all(isinstance(t, str) for t in value):
175	                    return "malformed"
176	            elif value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
177	                return "malformed"
178	        if node not in self.nodes:
179	            return "node_not_live"
180	        for field, value in changes.items():
181	            self.nodes[node][field] = list(value) if field == "tags" else value
182	            self.writes[(node, field)] = (seq, actor)
183	        return None
184	
185	    def _add_edge(self, seq: int, op: dict[str, Any], actor: str) -> str | None:
186	        f, t, kind = self._text(op, "from_id"), self._text(op, "to_id"), op.get("type")
187	        if f is None or t is None or kind not in EDGE_TYPES:
188	            return "malformed"
189	        if f not in self.nodes or t not in self.nodes:
190	            return "endpoint_not_live"
191	        problem = self._new_arrow_problem((f, t, kind))
192	        if problem:
193	            return problem
194	        self._add((f, t, kind), seq, actor)
195	        return None
196	
197	    def _repoint(self, seq: int, op: dict[str, Any], actor: str) -> str | None:
198	        f, t, kind = self._text(op, "from_id"), self._text(op, "to_id"), op.get("type")
199	        if f is None or t is None or kind not in EDGE_TYPES:
200	            return "malformed"
201	        new_from, new_to = op.get("new_from_id"), op.get("new_to_id")
202	        if (new_from is None) == (new_to is None):
203	            return "malformed"
204	        moved = self._text(op, "new_from_id" if new_from is not None else "new_to_id")
205	        if moved is None:
206	            return "malformed"
207	        new_edge = (moved, t, kind) if new_from is not None else (f, moved, kind)
208	        if not self.has_edge((f, t, kind)):
209	            return "edge_not_live"
210	        if moved not in self.nodes:
211	            return "endpoint_not_live"
212	        problem = self._new_arrow_problem(new_edge, child_moves=new_from is not None)
213	        if problem:
214	            return problem
215	        self._remove((f, t, kind), seq, actor)
216	        self._add(new_edge, seq, actor)
217	        return None
218	
219	    def _ingest(self, seq: int, op: dict[str, Any], actor: str) -> str | None:
220	        if actor != "ingest":
221	            return "actor_not_allowed"
222	        if any(field in op for field in AUTHORED):
223	            return "ingest_sets_authored_field"
224	        name, node_type, parent_name = self._text(op, "qualified_name"), self._text(op, "type"), op.get("parent")
225	        if name is None or node_type is None or (parent_name is not None and not isinstance(parent_name, str)):
226	            return "malformed"
227	        if name in self.by_name:
228	            node = self.by_name[name]
229	            self.nodes[node]["type"] = node_type
230	            self.writes[(node, "type")] = (seq, actor)
231	            return None
232	        node = ingest_node_id(op["op_id"], name)
233	        self.nodes[node] = {"qualified_name": name, "type": node_type, "description": None, "owner": None, "tags": []}
234	        self.by_name[name] = node
235	        self.writes[(node, "type")] = (seq, actor)
236	        if parent_name and parent_name in self.by_name:
237	            self._add((self.by_name[parent_name], node, "contains"), seq, actor)
238	        return None
239	
240	    def _delete(self, seq: int, op: dict[str, Any], actor: str) -> str | None:
241	        root = self._text(op, "root_id")
242	        if root is None:
243	            return "malformed"
244	        if root not in self.nodes:
245	            return "node_not_live"
246	        ids = self.subtree(root)
247	        doomed = set(ids)
248	        snapshot = {node: {**self.nodes[node], "parent": self.parent.get(node)} for node in ids}
249	        removed = {(self.parent[n], n, "contains") for n in ids if n in self.parent}
250	        removed |= {(f, t, "references") for f, t in self.refs if f in doomed or t in doomed}
251	        for edge in sorted(removed):
252	            self._remove(edge, seq, actor)
253	        for node in ids:
254	            del self.by_name[self.nodes.pop(node)["qualified_name"]]
255	            self.node_removals[node].append((seq, actor))
256	        self.deletes[op["op_id"]] = {"seq": seq, "nodes": snapshot, "edges": removed}
257	        return None
